query: rewrite this essay in the style of Harmonie Korine, Hello all, just a quick note on me and my AI journey. It all began in the fall of 2022 when a friend (shout out to the homey Chris) alerted me to this new magical AI application called Midjourney. It would blow me away he told me, allow me to create my own illustrations of whatever my mind could conjure, in whatever style I could imagine. That one conversation took me down an AI art rabbit hole I have yet to emerge from! Since then I have used AI applications (Kaiber, Moonvalley, Pika, Runway, Play HT, DiD, along with my Adobe Suite and self taught design skills) to create everything from Murals, to Comic Books, 100's of T-Shirt Designs, Music Videos, Flyers, Animated Shorts, Animated Sequences for Documentaries and TV Shows, Graphics, Interstitials, tons of Social Media Content and more. In addition I have taught what I've learned in classes with youth and adults on the Caribbean island of Montserrat and at the University of North Florida. While I've covered wide areas of AI usage in art, video and sound, the one area that I had yet to enter successfully was the utilization of AI to write a script. I had attempted this a year ago when the tech wasn't quite ready and I didn't have a technique. I was writing a spec script on the life of John and Alice Coltrane. I asked AI to write me a scene featuring John and Alice Coltrane having an argument about his drug use in their kitchen. The AI ended up interpreting the "John" in my prompt as "John Travolta" and the "Alice" as "Alice in Wonderland". 5 pages of this junk. While interesting on the face of it, greatly frustrating and time wasting. This is what is called a "hallucination", when an AI model generates incorrect information but presents it as if it were a fact. Being as how I was writing a historical script, facts were invaluable to the process. So needless to say, I abandoned that potential boondoggle. But something was about to change. On a whim one month ago, I decided to apply for a potentially life changing opportunity. It is a grant for Latino writers who had a show concept in the drama genre featuring a Latino lead. 6 people are chosen to receive it and the winners get to pitch their show ideas before professional show runners and a big network. I found about about this with one week left before the application window was closing so I quickly got to work. Luckily I had written an entire Bible (a reference document used by screenwriters for information on characters, settings, and other elements of a film project) for a show idea 3 years ago that genre wise fit this contest well enough. It is called "Electro Is Dead" and without getting too deep into the plot basically, it is "The summer of 1988 in Venice Beach, CA. Dennis Juarez aka DJ Rey, Afro-Chicano teen Electro DJ, becomes enmeshed into a dark plot to bring about Hell on Earth."
reference: Hey, wanderers and dreamers, gather 'round for the tale of my journey, a kaleidoscopic trip down the AI art rabbit hole that's as twisted and filled with neon colors as a story torn from the mind of Harmonie Korine. It all kicked off in the autumn haze of 2022, when a homie of mine, Chris (big ups, wherever your spirit roams), whispered into my ear about a digital Pandora's box named Midjourney. He was all like, "This is gonna flip your lid, man. It's like, summoning visions straight outta your brain's wildest corners into the solid world, in any freakin' style you dig." And, man, was he not peddling dreams. That chat? Well, it flung me head-first into an AI art abyss. And, pals, I've been free-falling through this wonderland ever since, crafting murals that blend the real with the surreal, comic books that drip with unspoken truths, shirts that speak louder than words, and music videos that are pure visual symphonies. You name it: flyers, animated tales shorter than a heartbeat yet as deep as the ocean, sequences that bring life to docos and TV without missing a beat, interstitials that bind the void, all wrought from the Pandora's box and my own two hands, shaped by sweat and pixel. Sharing this magic, I've been a digital shaman, guiding both young souls and wise travelers through this neon-lit path in Montserrat's embraced warmth and under the watchful eyes of the University of North Florida's halls. Spreading the AI gospel, from visuals to tunes, yet there was one dragon I hadn't slain: the beast of AI-scripted drama. Once, in the naive days of yore (like, a year back), I dared to dream of scripting a tale lit by John and Alice Coltrane's love and strife, set against the backdrop of his dance with vice. I whispered my wishes into AI's ear, only for it to spin me a yarn of John Travolta and Alice (yeah, from Wonderland) caught in a tempest in a teapot. Five pages of pure, unadulterated... fabrications. Intriguing? Perhaps. Utterly useless for my cause? Absolutely. They call this a "hallucination," a mirage in a desert thirsting for truth. My quest for historical fidelity was mocked by this absurd comedy of errors. But, as fate would dance in its mysterious ways, a spark ignited a new dream. On a whim, fueled by whispers of destiny, I hurled my hopes into a contest that sang songs to my soul, a grant destined for Latino scribes itching to paint dramas with strokes bold and true, starring Latino leads. With the sands of time bleeding away, I resurrected "Electro Is Dead," a testament I had penned in a bygone era. Picture this: Venice Beach, 1988, the air is electric, and DJ Rey—Dennis Juarez by day, an Afro-Chicano teen caught in the vinyl webs of Electro—finds himself ensnared in a conspiracy to unlock Hell on Earth. Wild, right? So, here I stand, at the precipice of tomorrow, my tale in hand, ready to dive headlong into whatever madcap, technicolor dream awaits. The journey? Far from over. The destination? Unknown. But the ride, dear friends, promises to be nothing short of spectacular. Join me, won’t you?

query: Story prompt: It is 1908. Irish author Bram Stoker is made aware of a seemingly insignificant series of short novels that have gained positive attraction. The novels consist of a morally grey heroic figure and their travels across the world. Despite the original character and unique setting, it was everything else that wasn’t original. The hero encountered the likes of Sherlock Holmes, a character created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. In other instances, this figure traveled through time with the very same time machine featured in H.G. Wells' story "The Time Machine", or perhaps traveled alongside Ebenezer Scrooge. This author even wrote stories where his character and Sherlock Holmes involved in the affairs of the Jane Austen novel "Pride and Prejudice" and did battles with Mr. Hyde or encountering Frankenstein’s monster from Mary Shelly's "Frankenstein" and Count Dracula, Stoker’s own creation. Instead of being standalone stories, an unknown author had thought to mix his own original ideas with the works of others.
reference:
# The Unlicensed Gentleman

*London, October 1908*

Bram Stoker had long ago learned to read the post standing up. Sitting meant committing, and a man who managed the Lyceum Theatre for Henry Irving's whims did not commit to anything before noon.

The parcel from Hatchard's was not post, though. It was a gift from Florence Balcombe, his wife, who had a talent for noticing what he hadn't yet noticed. A pamphlet-sized novel with a lurid yellow cover was wedged beneath the invoices. Her note read: *Read page forty. Then sit down.*

The cover read: ***The Marquess of Nowhere, and the Whitechapel Affair.***

He stood through the first thirty pages. At page forty he sat.

---

The hero was a man named Caspian Vane, a former surgeon who had left the Army and several other obligations behind him. He was a thief by trade, a healer by habit, and a liar by principle. He wore a gray greatcoat and carried a cane with a hollow core. He was, Stoker admitted grudgingly, an excellent creation. He was neither gentleman nor villain, and he had a way of making a bad decision feel like the only honorable one.

On page forty, Vane stood in a Baker Street sitting room, being politely and thoroughly deduced by a tall man with a pipe.

*"You've been in Afghanistan, Mr. Vane, or somewhere that wished to resemble it. You favor your left hand, though you were taught to use your right. And you have lied to me three times since you sat down, which is two fewer than I expected."*

*"I was nervous,"* said Vane.

*"You were not,"* said Holmes, delighted.

Stoker set the book down. Then he picked it up again, because it was good, and that was the trouble.

---

By evening he had found four more volumes in a shop on Charing Cross Road, where the clerk said they sold "steady, sir, to a quiet sort of reader." They bore the same yellow cover and the same anonymous byline: *By the Author of "The Marquess of Nowhere."*

He read through the night, with Florence's tea going cold at his elbow.

In ***The Marquess and the Chronic Argonauts*** (a nod, he noticed, to Wells's early title), Vane stole a brass-and-crystal machine from a Richmond laboratory. It was the very same Time Machine, down to the quartz levers and the nickel bars. He pursued a hooded Morlock sympathizer through the twilight of the year 802,701, then returned in time to apologize to the Time Traveller for the dent.

In ***A Christmas Debt***, Vane haunted the haunted. He sat beside Ebenezer Scrooge in the dark, not as a spirit but as an auditor, and quietly checked the ghosts' arithmetic. *"Marley's figures,"* Vane told the miser, *"were never right. He cheated you, too. It's the one thing the two of you shared."*

In ***Vanity and Vane***, Holmes and Vane were tangled together in the affairs of Longbourn and Netherfield. Mr. Darcy's first proposal was nearly derailed by a blackmail ring, and Elizabeth Bennet spent a chapter interrogating both detectives with such ferocity that Holmes confessed, in a footnote, to being outmatched.

In ***The Hyde Contention***, Vane fought Hyde on a fog-bound Soho rooftop. In ***The Modern Prometheus Ledger***, he sat with Frankenstein's creature on an Arctic ice floe and argued about whether a soul could be stolen or only misplaced.

Stoker laughed at that one, loudly enough that Florence called down the stairs to ask if he was ill.

---

The fifth book was ***The Marquess and the Count***, and he saved it until dawn.

He knew what he'd find, and still it unsettled him to find it. There was Castle Dracula, rendered faithfully. There was the Count, with his courtesy, his ancient cold hospitality, and his dreadful patience. Whoever wrote this had read *Dracula* closely, and had loved it.

Vane arrived at the castle not as Harker had, a naive solicitor, but as a professional. He brought garlic, a mirror, and a revolver he did not expect to work. The Count received him with delight.

*"You are not afraid,"* said Dracula.

*"I'm terrified,"* said Vane. *"I just don't see why that should stop me."*

Stoker read that line three times. It was, he thought, better than anything Harker had said. That stung.

---

He spent the next week in a state he could not name. It wasn't quite fury. He had friends who'd been plagiarized outright, and he knew that feeling, hot and clean. This was stranger. No one had stolen his Count. They had *borrowed* him, the way one borrows a coat for an evening, and returned him unharmed, perhaps slightly better pressed.

He wrote to Conan Doyle, who replied in four days from Windlesham with characteristic bluntness:

*My dear Stoker,*

*Yes, I know them. My secretary brought them to me in a state of high alarm. I read the Holmes one in an afternoon and was furious for the first half and flattered for the second. The man writes Holmes better than I do on my bad days, which, as you know, are frequent. I have no idea who he is. I've asked Greenhough Smith at the Strand, and he claims ignorance, though he lies badly.*

*Consult your solicitor if you like. Mine says we have no case worth the fee. The characters are ours, but the story, God help us, is his.*

*Yours, A.C.D.*

Stoker folded the letter and looked at the five yellow books lined up on his desk.

---

It took him a month and a favor from a printer in Fleet Street to find the publisher: a small firm called Penhallow & Reade, in a Clerkenwell alley. The office was a single room with a single clerk, who said the author sent his manuscripts through the post, unsigned, with payment instructions to a bank in Dublin.

"Dublin," said Stoker.

"Yes, sir."

"May I leave a letter?"

The clerk considered it, then shrugged. "He collects his post on Thursdays."

Stoker wrote it standing at the counter, which was how he did everything that mattered:

*Sir,*

*I am the author of one of the characters you have been so free with. I am not writing to threaten you. I confess I don't know why I am writing at all.*

*Your Vane would have asked a better question than mine, so I will borrow his: what do you want from us?*

*B. Stoker*

---

The reply came eleven days later. It was a single page, in a cramped and elegant hand, with no return address.

*Mr. Stoker,*

*Thank you for the courtesy of your letter. I expected a solicitor's.*

*You ask what I want. I will tell you honestly, since you asked honestly.*

*I grew up poor, in a house with eleven books. Eleven. I read them until the bindings broke, and then I read them from memory. When I was twelve, I understood that the people in them would never meet. Holmes would never see Dracula's castle. Scrooge would never sit with Darcy. They lived in separate rooms of the world and would die there, and I could not bear it.*

*So I built a door. Vane is the door. He is not meant to be remembered. He is meant to let the others walk through.*

*I know I am a thief. I have stolen nothing I did not love. If you wish to stop me, you may, and I will not contest it. But I would ask you first to read the last chapter of the Dracula book again, and tell me whether I have wronged him.*

*Yours in debt,*
*—The Author*

---

Stoker read the last chapter again that night.

In it, Vane stood on the battlements at dawn, with the Count wounded and weary and, for a moment, almost kind. *"You could have killed me a dozen times,"* Vane said. *"Why didn't you?"*

*"Because you came as a guest,"* said Dracula. *"No one has done so in four hundred years. Even monsters are lonely, Mr. Vane."*

Stoker put the book down. He had never written that line. He had never thought it. But looking at it now, he could not say it was wrong.

He sat in the dark for a long time. Then he took out his pen, and for the first time in years he did not write a letter, a ledger entry, or a theatre bill.

He wrote:

*Sir,*

*Do not stop. But next time, let me read it before the printer does. There is a thing about the Count you have not yet understood, and I should like to show you.*

*And for God's sake, give Vane a better cane.*

*B.S.*

He posted it himself, in the cold, before he could reconsider.

---

*Epilogue*

Bram Stoker died in 1912. Among his papers, his wife found a bundle of letters in a cramped, elegant hand, along with six yellow-covered novels, the last of which had been published three months after his death, with a dedication on its first page:

*For B.S., who held the door.*

The Author was never identified.

Materials and Methods: Retrospective screening was performed on patients with brain injuries who underwent CVVH at Xijing Hospital between 1 December 2010 and 31 December 2021 and who have a diagnosis of severe hypernatremia. The outcomes included 28-day patient mortality and hospital stay duration. The patient survival rate was examined using the Kaplan-Meier survival curve. To determine the risk factors for short-term death for patients, univariate and multivariate Cox regression analysis models were used. Results: Our current study included a total of 83 individuals. The included patients had a median age of 49 (IQR 35-59) years. Of the included patients, 58 patients (69.9%) died within 28 days. Conclusions: Brain injuries who have severe hypernatremia requires CVVH, which has high short-term patient mortality. Mechanical ventilation, INR increase, stroke, and vasopressor dependence are independently associated with increased patient mortality risk.

The hero encountered the likes of Sherlock Holmes, a character created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. In other instances, this figure traveled through time with the very same time machine featured in H.G. Wells' story "The Time Machine", or perhaps traveled alongside Ebenezer Scrooge. This author even wrote stories where his character and Sherlock Holmes involved in the affairs of the Jane Austen novel "Pride and Prejudice" and did battles with Mr. Hyde or encountering Frankenstein’s monster from Mary Shelly's "Frankenstein" and Count Dracula, Stoker’s own creation. reference:
# The Uninvited Guest

*London, October 1908*

Bram Stoker had not intended to buy the book. He had gone into the shop on Cecil Court looking for a birthday gift for his son Noel, and the bookseller, a stooped man with ink-stained cuffs, had pressed a slim volume into his hands.

"You'll want this one, Mr. Stoker. You're in it."

"I beg your pardon?"

"Well, not *you*." The bookseller coughed. "Your Count is."

The cover was cheap, a lurid yellow with a figure in a long grey coat standing on a rooftop against a red moon. The title read *The Gentleman from Nowhere and the Transylvanian Affair*. The author was given only as "A. Wanderer, Esq."

Stoker read it that night in his study, with the gas turned low and a glass of whiskey sweating at his elbow. He meant to read a chapter. He finished it at three in the morning and sat motionless as the fire died.

The hero was called Corvin Hale, a smuggler, occasional assassin, and reluctant conscience, who drifted through the world's ports with a sardonic wit and a debt to someone he never named. He was not a good man. He was not quite a bad one. He lied easily and kept the promises that mattered. Stoker found, to his irritation, that he liked him very much.

What troubled him was the Count.

It was *his* Count, the cadence of the speech, the courtesy that was itself a threat, even the detail of the castle's crumbling east stair. Yet it was not a copy. This Dracula was weary, almost courtly in his loneliness, and Hale bargained with him over a chessboard instead of a stake. Stoker had never imagined the Count could be *bargained* with, and the idea unsettled him because it worked.

---

Over the following weeks he hunted down the rest. There were eleven volumes in all, cheaply printed by a house in Holborn that no longer seemed to exist.

In *The Gentleman and the Fog*, Hale stood in a Baker Street sitting room and out-deduced Sherlock Holmes on a single point, a point so small and so *right* that Stoker laughed aloud. Holmes, to his credit, took it gracefully. Doyle himself might have written the scene, if Doyle had been willing to let Holmes be wrong.

In *The Gentleman and the Hours*, Hale stole a ride in Wells's Time Machine, much to the Time Traveller's fury, and spent three chapters stranded among the Eloi, trying to explain to them the concept of a lie.

In *A Christmas Debt*, he sat beside Scrooge at the foot of a bed and watched a ghost, and the book never said what Hale saw, only that he left before dawn and did not speak for a day.

There was a farcical volume in which Hale and Holmes blundered through the drawing rooms of *Pride and Prejudice*, scandalizing Mrs. Bennet and being quietly seen through by Elizabeth in a single glance. There was a grim one in which Hale stood over the wreckage of Frankenstein's laboratory and argued with the creature about whether a soul could be earned. There was Hyde, in an alley, in the rain.

Stoker thought: *This is theft.*

Then, more honestly: *This is theft done with love.*

---

He could not leave it alone. He wrote to the Holborn publisher and the letter came back unopened. He asked at the shops and received shrugs. At last, through an old friend at the Lyceum, he learned that the books sold steadily, never spectacularly, and that readers wrote to the vanished publisher asking for more.

"Clerks read them," his friend said. "Shop girls. Soldiers' wives. My cook. They pass them around like gossip."

"They're not original."

"No," his friend agreed. "But they're *alive*, Bram. You must admit it."

Stoker did not admit it. He went home and, after a long hour, took down his own copy of *Dracula* and reread the final chapters. Then he placed it beside Hale's adventure and compared the two as a jeweler might compare a stone with its reflection.

He realized, slowly, what bothered him. It was not that the author had borrowed the Count. Every writer borrows. It was that the borrowing had been *accurate*. Whoever wrote these books had read *Dracula* as Stoker had meant it to be read, had understood the fear beneath the fangs, and had then dared to ask what happened if someone simply sat down across from the monster and talked.

He had never dared ask that. He had been too frightened of the answer.

---

The letter arrived in November, in a plain envelope with no return address.

*Dear Mr. Stoker,*

*I expect you are angry. You have every right to be. I took your Count without leave, and Mr. Doyle's detective, and Mr. Wells's machine, and I will answer for it if I must.*

*But I was a lonely child in a house with few books, and those stories were my only companions. I could not bear that they should end when the last page did. So I invited a stranger into them, to see whether they would hold. They did. That is how I knew they were true.*

*I have written nothing else, and will write nothing else. The twelfth volume will be the last. I would be honored, though I do not expect it, if you would read it before it is printed.*

*Yours in debt,*
*A. W.*

A manuscript was enclosed. The title page read *The Gentleman and the Last Door.*

---

Stoker sat for a long while with the pages in his lap. Outside, the fog pressed against the window like something waiting to be let in.

He thought of lawyers, and of the principle of the thing. He thought of the nights he had spent building Castle Dracula stone by stone from borrowed maps and a Whitby gravestone and a name half-remembered from a library book. Nothing is born from nothing, he thought. Not even a vampire.

He lit the lamp and began to read.

By dawn he had reached the final chapter, where Corvin Hale at last stood before the door he had been walking toward through eleven books, and knocked, and was answered by a tired old man in a Dublin study who looked up from his desk and said, *Ah. There you are. I wondered when you'd come.*

Stoker put down the pages. His hands were not quite steady.

He took up his pen, and below the final line, in the margin, he wrote a single word:

*Granted.*

query: rewrite this essay in the style of Harmonie Korine, Hello all, just a quick note on me and my AI journey. It all began in the fall of 2022 when a friend (shout out to the homey Chris) alerted me to this new magical AI application called Midjourney. It would blow me away he told me, allow me to create my own illustrations of whatever my mind could conjure, in whatever style I could imagine. That one conversation took me down an AI art rabbit hole I have yet to emerge from! Since then I have used AI applications (Kaiber, Moonvalley, Pika, Runway, Play HT, DiD, along with my Adobe Suite and self taught design skills) to create everything from Murals, to Comic Books, 100's of T-Shirt Designs, Music Videos, Flyers, Animated Shorts, Animated Sequences for Documentaries and TV Shows, Graphics, Interstitials, tons of Social Media Content and more. In addition I have taught what I've learned in classes with youth and adults on the Caribbean island of Montserrat and at the University of North Florida. While I've covered wide areas of AI usage in art, video and sound, the one area that I had yet to enter successfully was the utilization of AI to write a script. I had attempted this a year ago when the tech wasn't quite ready and I didn't have a technique. I was writing a spec script on the life of John and Alice Coltrane. I asked AI to write me a scene featuring John and Alice Coltrane having an argument about his drug use in their kitchen. The AI ended up interpreting the "John" in my prompt as "John Travolta" and the "Alice" as "Alice in Wonderland". 5 pages of this junk. While interesting on the face of it, greatly frustrating and time wasting. This is what is called a "hallucination", when an AI model generates incorrect information but presents it as if it were a fact. Being as how I was writing a historical script, facts were invaluable to the process. So needless to say, I abandoned that potential boondoggle. But something was about to change. On a whim one month ago, I decided to apply for a potentially life changing opportunity. It is a grant for Latino writers who had a show concept in the drama genre featuring a Latino lead. 6 people are chosen to receive it and the winners get to pitch their show ideas before professional show runners and a big network. I found about about this with one week left before the application window was closing so I quickly got to work. Luckily I had written an entire Bible (a reference document used by screenwriters for information on characters, settings, and other elements of a film project) for a show idea 3 years ago that genre wise fit this contest well enough. It is called "Electro Is Dead" and without getting too deep into the plot basically, it is "The summer of 1988 in Venice Beach, CA. Dennis Juarez aka DJ Rey, Afro-Chicano teen Electro DJ, becomes enmeshed into a dark plot to bring about Hell on Earth."
reference: Hey, wanderers and dreamers, gather 'round for the tale of my journey, a kaleidoscopic trip down the AI art rabbit hole that's as twisted and filled with neon colors as a story torn from the mind of Harmonie Korine. It all kicked off in the autumn haze of 2022, when a homie of mine, Chris (big ups, wherever your spirit roams), whispered into my ear about a digital Pandora's box named Midjourney. He was all like, "This is gonna flip your lid, man. It's like, summoning visions straight outta your brain's wildest corners into the solid world, in any freakin' style you dig." And, man, was he not peddling dreams. That chat? Well, it flung me head-first into an AI art abyss. And, pals, I've been free-falling through this wonderland ever since, crafting murals that blend the real with the surreal, comic books that drip with unspoken truths, shirts that speak louder than words, and music videos that are pure visual symphonies. You name it: flyers, animated tales shorter than a heartbeat yet as deep as the ocean, sequences that bring life to docos and TV without missing a beat, interstitials that bind the void, all wrought from the Pandora's box and my own two hands, shaped by sweat and pixel. Sharing this magic, I've been a digital shaman, guiding both young souls and wise travelers through this neon-lit path in Montserrat's embraced warmth and under the watchful eyes of the University of North Florida's halls. Spreading the AI gospel, from visuals to tunes, yet there was one dragon I hadn't slain: the beast of AI-scripted drama. Once, in the naive days of yore (like, a year back), I dared to dream of scripting a tale lit by John and Alice Coltrane's love and strife, set against the backdrop of his dance with vice. I whispered my wishes into AI's ear, only for it to spin me a yarn of John Travolta and Alice (yeah, from Wonderland) caught in a tempest in a teapot. Five pages of pure, unadulterated... fabrications. Intriguing? Perhaps. Utterly useless for my cause? Absolutely. They call this a "hallucination," a mirage in a desert thirsting for truth. My quest for historical fidelity was mocked by this absurd comedy of errors. But, as fate would dance in its mysterious ways, a spark ignited a new dream. On a whim, fueled by whispers of destiny, I hurled my hopes into a contest that sang songs to my soul, a grant destined for Latino scribes itching to paint dramas with strokes bold and true, starring Latino leads. With the sands of time bleeding away, I resurrected "Electro Is Dead," a testament I had penned in a bygone era. Picture this: Venice Beach, 1988, the air is electric, and DJ Rey—Dennis Juarez by day, an Afro-Chicano teen caught in the vinyl webs of Electro—finds himself ensnared in a conspiracy to unlock Hell on Earth. Wild, right? So, here I stand, at the precipice of tomorrow, my tale in hand, ready to dive headlong into whatever madcap, technicolor dream awaits. The journey? Far from over. The destination? Unknown. But the ride, dear friends, promises to be nothing short of spectacular. Join me, won’t you?

And Mr bear her gets the aisle seat , huh?” Max winked at Lily, her entire face enlightening with the promise of a jovial, healthy day, her pulse steady, her respiration clear and sparkling with life. Whether it is "overwrought" can be a subjective assessment, depending on the context within the larger narrative and the intended effect on the reader. Overwrought writing is often characterized by being excessively complex, overly dramatic, or laden with too many embellishments, which can detract from the clarity or believability of the prose. In this case, there are places where the prose feels quite dense with metaphors and descriptive details ("My bean is now a little cucumber"), but it also gives a vivid impression of Max's relief and joy at his daughter's recovery and the impending return home. The intent seems to be to create an intense emotional experience, reflecting both the chaotic environment of the hospital and the personal drama of Max's situation. Whether it succeeds or is overwrought may depend on the reader's preference for descriptive writing as well as the pacing and tone of the surrounding text in the actual narrative. If the aim is to portray the intensity of Max's feelings without overwhelming the reader, the passage might benefit from a slight simplification, focusing on the most essential and impactful details. However, if the style fits with the rest of the work and serves to enhance the storytelling, it may be well-suited to the narrative as is.

query: Write a 250-word introduction for the following essay: Change Proposal #1: Foster Personal Connections to HHV Health and Human Values is a minor that aims to foster growth of individuals as they pursue careers in health and health care. It prompts students to reflect on issues related to health with an interdisciplinary lens and think about how they can make an impact now and in the future. HHV is not intended to purely be a stepping stone to medical school or graduate school. However, some students state that they are in HHV because it will look good on their resume. In addition, many students express frustration with the assignments in HNRS 250 and do not understand how the readings and reflections connect to their journey in the minor. Another challenge is that sometimes students may conform to the values expressed by Dr. Braitberg or other professors rather than articulating their own opinion. We suggest that HHV make changes that prompt students to develop personal connections to their work in the minor. One change to foster personal connections is to integrate group values into HHV starting in the HNRS 250 class. Group values are a set of beliefs held by a group of people that inform their actions as they work together. By creating group values among each cohort and HHV as a whole, students will feel that their work in HHV is more meaningful to them and will be more invested in the program. Establishing group agreements as students begin HNRS 250 is a great way to start integrating group values in HHV. Group agreements are a set of rules agreed to by the group to create a learning environment in which students are comfortable and enthusiastic engaging in. Examples of group agreements in PATH are Listen Actively, Build the Change, and Uphold Confidentiality. Dr. Braitberg, Dr. Oberman, or other professors teaching HNRS 250 should first prompt students to reflect on what their personal values are which could include Integrity, Justice, and Health. Students can then have discussions about their individual values as a class and make connections with the values of the group and the minor. Then, the professors should have the students brainstorm group agreements that integrate group values. A challenge to this exercise may be that students will be reluctant to participate, especially as underclassmen. The professors can initiate the discussion and make connections between the values of students, but they should be careful not to dominate the activity. These group agreements should be practiced throughout HNRS 250. In addition, there should be more assignments and readings in HNRS 250, the capstone, and internship that require students to reflect on their individual and group values and how they relate to issues in health and healthcare. If students find their own values integrated more in HHV, they will be more invested and engaged as well as find value in the program beyond being a stepping stone. Change Proposal #2: Create More Experiential Learning Opportunities in the Minor The HHV minor places a focus on understanding the social, ethical, cultural, political, and structural factors shape health, disease, and health care. Such an understanding, especially that of an interdisciplinary nature, requires students to be able to critically think about different social issues related to health care. However, one of the concerns with regard to the HHV minor is that there is less student engagement, and one of the reasons for this decreased engagement may be that students sometimes may struggle to understand how the content they are learning in their HHV classes applies directly to their future careers or the communities, institutions, and other settings they are part of in the real-world. Such confusion or lack of understanding can also decrease student engagement. One of the ways to foster critical thinking as well as increase student engagement is through creating more experiential learning opportunities in the minor. Students really value the opportunity to speak with people from different community organizations that address different issues like poverty, homelessness, disability justice, etc that are discussed in the HHV classes. Having an opportunity to speak to more guest speakers can enable students to more clearly see how the content they discuss in class can be applied to the real-world and thus engage with the minor and peers more often. Through experiential learning opportunities such as volunteering and service learning, students will also have the chance to interact with different people and communities that experience the social and health issues discussed in class. This will increase students’ empathy and understanding as well as foster a passion for justice and creating change. Ultimately, experiential learning can increase students’ feelings of citizenship in the minor and ability to think about creating organic change within their own communities. Additionally, students may sometimes feel overwhelmed with too many readings and the same class structure for every class, which can also lead to decreased engagement. One way to potentially address this issue is to prioritize quality over quantity. For instance, organizing field trips to different community organizations (especially for the 250 class) in place of some regular class readings and discussions can allow students to engage with class content in a different learning environment, which can also help increase engagement and allow for a deeper understanding and connection to course material. Furthermore, creating opportunities for meaningful reflections after such experiences can enable students to reflect on their personal growth and consider numerous other career opportunities both in and outside of healthcare to address the issues they are most passionate about. Change Proposal #3: Improve Organization and Structure of HHV Classes We would like to propose an increase in overall structure and organization of the Health and Human Values classes. Establishing a clear structure that is well organized gives students peace of mind and helps them succeed academically. An essential part of any relationship is setting clear expectations of each party. In the context of a student-teacher relationship, a teacher needs to establish their expectations of the student for their class. We would recommend that a syllabus is established by the first day of class. This way, the student is able to fully understand what is expected of them from the beginning. The student can plan accordingly and ensure that the class is the right fit for them and their schedule. We also recommend that the syllabus remain relatively consistent throughout the semester and within cohorts. This would provide students with a sense of stability in addition to clear expectations. Regarding the organization of classes, we recommend that classes follow a similar structure between cohorts. Something that we have noted as mentors is that when talking with mentees, it seems that the class structure has changed since we have taken the class. Although the core values of the HHV minor are always present, it may help give students peace of mind if they knew what to expect of the introduction and the capstone course. Developing a framework that each class follows could still allow for changes from year to year, but the framework would be able to give the class some consistency. The framework could be used by other professors in the future as well. Anonymous student feedback surveys may help Dr. Braitberg to learn more about what students would like to see from the organization and structure of the HHV minor. Although there is a university wide end of semester student course survey, we believe that Dr. Braitberg should have students fill out an anonymous survey that is more specific to the organization and structure of the class. This could provide Dr. Braitberg with more helpful insight into what students would like to see with regards to structure and organization. Change Proposal #4: Increase Inter-Cohort and Alumni Support/Connection The Health and Human values minor has a diverse group of majors, internships, and various opportunities that are available to the community. However, there are rarely settings where these are shared across cohorts. The first time that we were able to share our own opportunities/experiences in depth was as mentors in the 250 course. A potential way to enrich participation in the minor is through events where sharing these opportunities is celebrated and encouraged. Thus, HHV social events one or two every semester, where HHV students in the internship, capstone, and core introductory course are required to attend would start the spread of information about unique opportunities that are available in the healthcare space. Another method to increase the inter-cohort support by other undergraduate mentors would be an HHV preceptorship for the 250 course in the spring. A preceptorship encourages dialogue between more HHV seniors and newer students in the minor. A peer mentor has the advantage of being more approachable, the shared experience of being a student in the course, and could reduce the grading workload for faculty (for smaller assignments like discussion posts). When most people enter their internship, most talk to Dr. Braitberg and the person who previously was in the internship before them, but rarely get the opportunity to see presentations about internships that are available to them. Therefore, there should be a database of posters/recorded presentations that students can watch if they are unable to come to the peer capstone/internship academic poster session. The HHV minor has multiple graduating classes, but there seems to be a lack of alumni support from those that are outside of the minor. Therefore, it is imperative that alumni offer advice and support to students that are trying to find their path through the HHV minor and beyond. There should be a form/spreadsheet with the contact information of graduated HHV students along with a note (if possible) of what their plans were immediately after graduation. This would allow HHV mentors to start connecting with alumni near graduation and could become something that could be advertised to increase the amount of people that apply to HHV. HHV is an Honors minor, but there seems to be a limited connection between it and the remainder of the Honors College. An idea that should be discussed further is offering interdisciplinary approaches to problems by offering collaborative work sessions or seminars between HHV students and other Honors minors.
reference: Health and Human Values (HHV) is an interdisciplinary minor that seeks to cultivate well-rounded individuals as they venture into careers related to health and health care. With an emphasis on critical thinking and self-reflection, students are encouraged to examine health-related issues through various sociocultural, political, and ethical perspectives. This essay delves into the improvement of the HHV program with proposals geared towards enhancing personal connections, learning experiences, course structure, and alumni engagement. Enrolling in the HHV minor may sometimes be motivated by instrumental goals, such as gaining an advantage in medical or graduate school applications. To address this issue, experiential learning opportunities, such as interactions with community organizations, guest speakers, and field trips, can provide invaluable insight that bridges the gap between theory and practice. Furthermore, a well-structured and organized course enhances the academic experience for students. By providing a consistent and comprehensive syllabus that outlines clear expectations, students can better plan for their academic journey within the program. This consistency should extend to the class structure, where following a similar framework across cohorts can maintain the foundational values of the HHV minor. Lastly, fostering inter-cohort support and alumni connections can benefit students immensely. Through sharing experiences and broadening networks, current and past students can contribute to each other's success in various healthcare careers. In summary, implementing changes to enhance personal connections, experiential learning opportunities, course structure, and alumni connections will lead to a more enriching experience for all students engaging with the Health and Human Values minor.

query: Think a title for :Rose Alex was in my cabin, talking about the overall idea that I might be expecting from him. I told him all I have and he noted it down in a notepad when Sarah came to my office to call me for the outfit trials. I'm so glad to have her work for my secretory. Joseph was the one to recommend her for her efficient skills and poised demeanour as she talks with people. I have reasons to believe they’ve worked together in the past. Walking towards the trial rooms, I couldn't help but notice the tension radiating from Joseph as he watched Alex and I coming through. His irritated expression perplexed me, considering he had been the one to choose Alex as the director. He was even thankful earlier when Alex confirmed to give us dates for the shoots, as it deemed to me like a big deal. Why wouldn’t it be, Alex is known to be the best in the field. It seemed now that there was some unspoken history between them. Entering the room on the first floor, I observed racks of costumes neatly arranged on hangers, waiting to be tried on. The walls were adorned with sketches and fabric swatches, adding an artistic touch to the space. A full-length mirror stood in one corner, ready to reflect the transformation of the actors. Sean, the designer approached us, his tone slightly curt. “Rose, glad you could make it. We need your opinion on the costumes. The actors are waiting.” I nodded, acknowledging his request. “I'm eager to see the outfits myself. Let's get started.” The actors began trying on their costumes as Sean suggested. The first apparels they came out wearing formal patterns, shirts and long pants. “Light cotton fabrics with detailed embroidery and flowy patterns should suit more to the theme.” I observed.” Sean nodded, picking out the types of outfits I suggested from the hanger. Alex leaned in closer to me, a mischievous glimmer in his eyes. “Rose, you have a way of making even costume trials exciting. I can't help but admire your attention to detail.” I chuckled, feeling a slight blush creep onto my cheeks. “Well, it's all about creating the perfect look, isn't it? Every little detail matters.” Meanwhile, Joseph sat nearby, his crossed arms and furrowed brows indicating his displeasure. Alex, seemingly unfazed, couldn't resist teasing him. “Joseph, don't worry. I won't steal your spotlight. I'm just here to bring Rose's vision to life.” Joseph's response was curt. “Just make sure you do your job, Alex. That’s what we are paying you for.” I laughed awkwardly. “Let’s focus on work.” The tension between them was palpable, and I couldn't help but feel caught in the middle, like literally. If it wasn’t for work, I don’t think I will ever be able to handle them together. So, I focused on the actors, offering feedback on the costumes and engaging in lighthearted banter to lighten the mood. Oh completely, utterly useless. Emma twirled in her vibrant floral maxi dress, her eyes sparkling with excitement. “Rose, what do you think? Does this costume capture your vision of my character?” I examined her outfit, considering its fit and overall aesthetic. “Emma, you look stunning. The costume perfectly embodies your character. It's elegant yet approachable but I think there is something missing here. what do you think Alex?” “Yeah!” he nodded. Jake joined in, a mischievous grin on his face. “Rose, do you think this costume will make me look dashing enough to win over hearts?” I playfully rolled my eyes. “Jake, with your charm, you don't need a costume to win hearts. But yes, this one adds an extra touch of charisma.” As the actors continued trying on different outfits, Alex took the opportunity to talk playfully with me. “Rose, it really doesn’t seem like your first project. You seem to have a great foresight.” I blushed, trying to hide my smile, proud of what I've accomplished thanks to Joseph. But he is farther to happiness as he can be. He is sitting brooding for some reason. “Alex, you know how to charm a girl, don't you?” Sean teased. “But let's focus on the task at hand, shall we? There is a lot of work and much less time.” “Yes, Alex let’s work now. we can talk about other things later.” Joseph, seemingly unable to ignore our interaction, interjected. “We're here to work, not flirt, Alex.” Alex smirked, undeterred. “Joseph, no need to be jealous. You had your chance with Rose. It's my turn now.” My eyes widened in surprise, and I quickly redirected the conversation. “Alright, enough banter, gentlemen. Let's get back to the costumes. We need to ensure that every detail is perfect.” The costume trial continued amidst the playful exchanges and occasional jabs between Alex and Joseph. As we narrowed down the options and made final decisions, a sense of excitement and satisfaction filled inside me. Despite the underlying tension, I couldn't help but find the situation amusing. There was something comical about the contrasting personalities and their playful rivalry. One can't help but smile, other is sitting on the chair like a sulking child. While everyone else are talking and sharing opinions. The actors began trying on the chosen outfits, one after the other, swirling around to give us a good look. Sean carefully observed their fits, making minor adjustments here and there. Tweaking one safety pin behind or another on the side. Emma raised her concerns about the length of her dress, while Jake argued that his shirt felt too tight around the collar. There are many more adjustments that is gonna be needed for Sean to complete in a few days. In the midst of their debates, Joseph and Alex chimed in with their opinions. Joseph, ever the advocate for bold choices, insisted, “We need some vibrant shades to bring out the characters' personalities. We have very little time to showcase a story. it will be better if they can use the help of their outfits.” He is not wrong, but that would make them contrasted. We need to follow a color theme. Alex, on the other hand, countered, “I believe pastels and fresh colors are more in line with the current trends. It will give the production a modern touch.” Observing the two men on either side of me, I couldn't help but feel caught in the middle. I carefully considered their opinions before voicing my own. “I think Alex has a point. Pastels would indeed give a refreshing and contemporary vibe to the costumes. And since we are following a summer vibe, I think that should be considered.” A proud smile formed on Alex's lips, while Joseph's irritation was evident. However, before Joseph could express his dissent, his phone rang, and he excused himself to take the call. His sudden departure left an awkward silence in the room. Everyone adjust to the little awkwardness that still remained and started again with the work. Taking advantage of the moment, Alex leaned closer to me, a playful glimmer in his eyes. “Rose, I must say, your taste in fashion aligns perfectly with mine. I'm glad we're on the same page.” I chuckled, feeling a mixture of excitement and confusion. “It seems we have a shared aesthetic, Alex. Let's hope it translates well into the production.” Just as we were conversing, Joseph returned unexpectedly, his eyes narrowing as he witnessed us talking. A surge of anger flashed across his face before he abruptly turned and stormed back to his office, leaving us puzzled. The costume designer, sensing the tension, tried to diffuse the situation. “Well, Rose, Alex, the fittings are almost complete. Overall, I believe the costumes are shaping up wonderfully. The colors and styles complement the characters' personalities perfectly.” I nodded, grateful for the designer's input. “Thank you for your hard work. Please get started with the fittings. We’ll start filming from next week.” As the actors continued changing outfits to their clothes when Alex added, “how about we share contacts, I'll call you soon as my assistant confirm the location?” I hesitated for a moment, glancing around to ensure no prying eyes were watching, before sharing my contact information with him. Our exchange didn't go unnoticed by Joseph, who had returned to the room, his eyes fixed on us. His anger was palpable as he silently observed Alex's demeanor. His reaction perplexed me. I couldn't understand why he was acting so mad, especially considering he had chosen Alex as the director. His sudden withdrawal, retreating to his room for the rest of the discussion only added to my confusion. Despite the underlying tension, I tried to maintain a sense of professionalism. I engaged in discussions with the actors, providing feedback on the costumes and offering encouragement. However, the absence of Joseph's presence weighed heavily on the atmosphere. Done for the day, I couldn't help but feel a mixture of excitement and apprehension for the upcoming production. The dynamic between Alex and Joseph had certainly added an unexpected twist to the process. I could only hope that their differences would ultimately contribute to the success of the project, rather than hinder it. Everyone already went home when I walked into Joseph's office, holding the photographs of the chosen outfits and makeup styles in my hands. His reaction was far from what I expected. He simply nodded and took the photos without saying anything other than, “I'll see it.” Concern etched across my face, I couldn't help but wonder if he was sick. So, I asked, “Joseph, is something wrong? Are you feeling unwell?” He shook his head dismissively. “No, I'm fine. Just a bit preoccupied with work, that's all.” I sighed relief. I've been in the mistake of thinking that I've done something to annoy him. but if it isn’t for me, it must have something to do with Alex. Sensing his distance, I mustered up the courage to extend an invitation. “You know, Joseph, I've been meaning to thank you for everything you've done. How about I take you and Mark out for dinner? It'll be my treat.” He waved his hand, brushing off my offer. “No need to bother. You can go ahead with your plans for the date you've set up with Alex.” His response caught me off guard. Confusion clouded my thoughts as I searched for an explanation. “Joseph, I don't understand. Why are you acting this way? What do you mean by 'the date you’ve set up'? I'm not going on any date.” With mounting frustration, he unleashed his pent-up anger. His words cut through me like a sharp blade. “We are here for work, Rose! Not to indulge in romantic entanglements. Don't you get that? I've begged everyone because I saw potential in you, but for some days I'm seeing you are more occupied with something else.” His outburst left me speechless, my emotions teetering on the edge. I've been working even after leaving office. Still planning everything meticulously. How can his accusatory tone make me feel so disappointed. “Fine! If you are going to do this, I'll better leave you alone.” Unable to bear his accusations any longer, I quietly left his office and retreated to my own. The weight of his words lingered, leaving me with a sense of hurt and confusion. As I closed the door behind me, I sank into my chair, struggling to make sense of Joseph's sudden anger. What had I done to deserve such treatment? I had simply been trying to foster a positive working environment and extend my gratitude for all his help. The room felt suffocating, and I longed for answers. I couldn't help but question why Joseph's frustrations were being directed at me. Had I unknowingly crossed a boundary? The more I pondered, the more frustrated and disheartened I became. Feeling a mix of emotions, I resolved to give Joseph some space, hoping that he would eventually explain his outburst. It was clear that tensions were running high, and I had no desire to exacerbate the situation further. The silence enveloping me, I couldn't shake off the nagging feeling of confusion and disappointment. This unexpected turn of events had cast a shadow over our once harmonious working relationship, leaving me yearning for resolution and understanding. But for the day, I'm going to go home and not think about it anymore.
reference: Title: Unspoken Tension in the Costume Fitting Room: Rose's Confusion and Disappointment.

Craig Storti is an American author, trainer, and consultant in intercultural communication and cross-cultural adaptation. He is widely regarded as one of the more practical, accessible writers in the field.

query: 翻译下面的英文Due to their hydrophobic nature, pentacyclic triterpenoids are almost insoluble in water. They are classified in the biopharmaceutical classification system as class IV drugs as their pharmacological effects are limited due to their low solubility in water and potential difficulty in permeating biological membranes [78]. For these reasons, some new approaches have been introduced to enhance their biopharmaceutical properties, particularly drug delivery technologies. At present, nano-emulsions, mesoporous silica nanoparticles, solid lipid nanoparticles, liposomes, niossomal gels and solid dispersions have been proposed quite successfully [79]; however, most of these studies were performed in experimental animals, and research in humans is very scarce, despite the great therapeutic potential of these natural biocompounds. Table 1 summarizes the current knowledge of OA pharmacokinetics in humans after oral single-dose administration. Song et al. [80] reported the results of a pharmacokinetic study performed with 18 healthy male Chinese volunteers, in which the participants received a single dose of 40 mg OA (capsule preparation). Venous blood samples were collected for 48 h, and the plasma was analyzed for OA contents. The area under the plasma OA concentration–time curve (AUC) was determined in 124.3 ± 106.7 ng h/mL, with a peak OA concentration of 12.1 ± 6.8 ng/mL, which was registered at 5.2 ± 2.9 h after the OA intake. Later on, a randomized, crossover and self-control study was carried out with 18 healthy Chinese male volunteers, who received 20 mg OA orally, formulated as normal tablets and dispersible tablets [81]. The resulting pharmacokinetic parameters included AUC values of 112.2 ± 56.6 and 109.7 ± 41.6 ng h/mL, for normal and dispersible tablets, respectively, and OA peak concentrations of 18.9 ± 8.0 and 17.8 ± 7.5 ng/mL, which were recorded at 2.9 ± 1.2 and 2.5 ± 1.0 h after the triterpene administration. In 2015, Rada et al. informed on a pharmacokinetic study developed with nine adult men, who were administered 30 mg OA dissolved in 70 g of pomace olive oil. The reported AUC value was 3181.9 ± 894.3 ng h/mL, with an OA maximum concentration of 598.2 ± 176.7 ng/mL, achieved at 3.0 ± 0.8 h after the intake of the OA-containing oil. The administered OA dose revealed a distribution volume of 81.4 ± 9.7 L, and removal half-lives of 4.6 ± 1.1 h. The 30 mg OA oral dose yielded a total clearance of 35.1 ± 4.2 L/h [82]. More recently, de la Torre et al. [83] reported that an administration of 4.7 mg of OA within 30 mL of olive oil to 12 individuals led to a maximum concentration of 5.1 ± 2.1 ng/mL in plasma 4 h after the intake.

`Fernet(key)` needs a real key, which is 32 url-safe base64-encoded bytes, as produced by `Fernet.generate_key()`. There are several other bugs too:

1. You never call `generate_key()` or `load_key()`.
2. `generate_key()` writes the key to a file literally named `"input_file_path"` (in quotes) instead of a proper path.
3. The function parameters are confused. `encrypt_file` ignores its argument and reads the global `input_file_path`, and `decrypt_file` reads from and writes to the same file.
4. The docstrings use six quotes (`""""""`), which is messy.
5. You decrypt the wrong file. You should decrypt the *encrypted* file (Test2) into Test3.
6. The last step, encrypting again, is redundant.

## Fixed code

```python
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

input_file_path = r'C:\Users\Abu Bakr Siddique\Desktop\Test.txt'
encrypted_file_path = r'C:\Users\Abu Bakr Siddique\Desktop\Test2.txt'
decrypted_file_path = r'C:\Users\Abu Bakr Siddique\Desktop\Test3.txt'
key_file_path = r'C:\Users\Abu Bakr Siddique\Desktop\secret.key'


def generate_key():
    """Generates a key and saves it into a file."""
    key = Fernet.generate_key()
    with open(key_file_path, "wb") as key_file:
        key_file.write(key)
    return key


def load_key():
    """Loads the key from the key file."""
    with open(key_file_path, "rb") as key_file:
        return key_file.read()


def encrypt_file(source_path, dest_path, key):
    """Reads source_path, encrypts it, writes result to dest_path."""
    f = Fernet(key)
    with open(source_path, "rb") as file:
        file_data = file.read()
    encrypted_data = f.encrypt(file_data)
    with open(dest_path, "wb") as file:
        file.write(encrypted_data)


def decrypt_file(source_path, dest_path, key):
    """Reads source_path, decrypts it, writes result to dest_path."""
    f = Fernet(key)
    with open(source_path, "rb") as file:
        encrypted_data = file.read()
    decrypted_data = f.decrypt(encrypted_data)
    with open(dest_path, "wb") as file:
        file.write(decrypted_data)


# Create a key once (then you can use load_key() on later runs)
key = generate_key()
# key = load_key()

# Encrypt Test.txt -> Test2.txt
encrypt_file(input_file_path, encrypted_file_path, key)
print(f"{input_file_path} has been encrypted to {encrypted_file_path}.")

# Decrypt Test2.txt -> Test3.txt
decrypt_file(encrypted_file_path, decrypted_file_path, key)
print(f"{encrypted_file_path} has been decrypted to {decrypted_file_path}.")
```

## Notes

- **Keep the key file safe.** If you lose `secret.key`, you can't decrypt your data.
- Don't call `generate_key()` every run if you want to decrypt files from earlier runs, because a new key can't decrypt old data. Generate once, then use `load_key()`.
- If you later get `InvalidToken`, it means the key is wrong or the file being decrypted isn't Fernet-encrypted data.

reference:
# Business Plan: Italian Sandwich Food Truck, Warsaw

*All figures are estimates in PLN (EUR at roughly 4.3 PLN) based on typical 2024-25 market ranges. Get current quotes before committing.*

---

## 1. Concept

- **Product:** Freshly baked Italian breads (ciabatta, focaccia, schiacciata, piadina as an optional cheaper line) filled with premium Italian products: prosciutto di Parma, mortadella, provolone, burrata, nduja, sun-dried tomatoes, pesto, etc.
- **Positioning:** Premium street food, with a ticket of about 28-40 PLN per sandwich, aimed at office workers, students, and food-festival crowds.
- **Differentiator:** Bread baked in-house and a short menu of 6-8 sandwiches with authentic ingredients.

---

## 2. Setup Options

### Option A: Used food truck/trailer, with bread baked off-site
Bake in a rented commissary or partner kitchen, and use the truck only for assembly and sale.

| Item | Cost (PLN) |
|---|---|
| Used trailer/van, converted | 60,000-120,000 |
| Equipment (fridges, grill/panini press, small oven) | 10,000-25,000 |
| Commissary kitchen rental (monthly) | 2,500-6,000 |
| **Startup total** | **~75,000-150,000** |

### Option B: New custom-built truck with an onboard oven
| Item | Cost (PLN) |
|---|---|
| New build (van or trailer, fully fitted) | 150,000-300,000 |
| Convection or deck oven, proofer | 8,000-25,000 |
| **Startup total** | **~160,000-320,000** |

*Baking on board is difficult. Space, power/gas, and smell are all issues. Many operators bake elsewhere.*

### Option C: Own small production kitchen plus a lighter trailer/stall (recommended for scaling)
| Item | Cost (PLN) |
|---|---|
| Small premises lease and deposit | 10,000-25,000 |
| Fit-out, ventilation, sanitation | 20,000-60,000 |
| Bakery equipment (mixer, oven, proofer, bench) | 25,000-70,000 |
| Used trailer | 40,000-90,000 |
| **Startup total** | **~100,000-250,000** |

### Option D: Test first with a market stall or pop-up tent
| Item | Cost (PLN) |
|---|---|
| Tent, counter, small equipment | 5,000-15,000 |
| Commissary rental | 2,500-5,000/month |
| **Startup total** | **~10,000-25,000** |

This is the cheapest way to validate demand before buying a truck.

---

## 3. Other One-Time Costs (all options)

| Item | Cost (PLN) |
|---|---|
| Company registration (JDG is free via CEIDG; sp. z o.o. is about 600-2,500) | 0-2,500 |
| Sanepid (PIQS) registration/approval of the vehicle and premises | 0-500 (plus preparation costs) |
| HACCP/GHP documentation and training | 1,000-3,000 |
| Branding, logo, wrap for the truck | 3,000-12,000 |
| POS and online cash register (kasa fiskalna) | 1,500-4,000 |
| Insurance (annual) | 1,500-4,000 |
| Initial stock and packaging | 4,000-10,000 |
| Working capital buffer (3 months) | 20,000-40,000 |
| **Subtotal** | **~30,000-75,000** |

---

## 4. Warsaw Regulations

- **Registration:** Register a business (JDG or spółka) and choose PKD 56.10.B or 56.10.A (mobile food service).
- **Sanepid:** Notify the Państwowa Inspekcja Sanitarna and obtain approval for the vehicle.
- **Street trading permit:** Trading on public land requires a lease/permit from the city district (Zarząd Dróg Miejskich or the dzielnica). Warsaw restricts street trading in many areas, so **most trucks operate on private land, at events, or in food truck parks**.
- **Vehicle:** If it's a van, it needs technical registration changes (special-purpose vehicle). A trailer needs to meet the road-use rules.
- **Bread production:** If you bake, you fall under bakery rules, and the commissary must be approved.
- **Allergen labeling** is mandatory (EU 1169/2011).
- **Cash register:** An online fiscal register is required, and card payments must be offered.

Confirm the details with Sanepid and the district office, because local rules change.

---

## 5. Monthly Operating Costs

| Item | Estimate (PLN/month) |
|---|---|
| Ingredients (COGS about 30-35% of sales) | 12,000-25,000 |
| Commissary/premises rent | 2,500-8,000 |
| Fuel, gas, electricity | 1,000-2,500 |
| Event/food park pitch fees | 1,500-6,000 |
| Employee (1 part-time or full-time, incl. contributions) | 5,000-9,000 |
| Accounting | 400-900 |
| ZUS (owner, sole proprietor) | ~1,600-2,100 (preferential at the start is lower) |
| Insurance, marketing, misc. | 1,000-2,500 |
| **Total** | **~25,000-55,000** |

---

## 6. Revenue and Break-even

Assumptions: average ticket of 35 PLN, about 20 trading days per month.

| Scenario | Sandwiches/day | Monthly revenue |
|---|---|---|
| Low | 40 | ~28,000 |
| Medium | 70 | ~49,000 |
| High | 100 | ~70,000 |

- **Gross margin on ingredients:** Prosciutto di Parma and burrata are expensive. A sandwich with 60-80 g prosciutto costs about 10-14 PLN in ingredients and bread. Target a **food cost of 30-35%**.
- **Break-even:** About **60-80 sandwiches per trading day** under Option A or C, depending on fixed costs.
- **Payback:** Typically **18-36 months** for a truck. A pop-up is faster.

---

## 7. Sample Menu and Pricing

| Sandwich | Filling | Price (PLN) |
|---|---|---|
| Parma | Prosciutto di Parma, rocket, parmesan, olive oil | 36-42 |
| Provolone | Provolone, grilled vegetables, pesto | 30-34 |
| Mortadella | Mortadella, pistachio cream, stracciatella | 34-38 |
| Caprese | Mozzarella/burrata, tomato, basil | 30-34 |
| Piccante | Nduja, provolone, honey | 32-36 |
| Vegan | Grilled vegetables, hummus | 26-30 |

Add drinks (Italian sodas, espresso) and sides for extra margin.

---

## 8. Sourcing

- Importers/wholesalers in Poland: Italian specialty distributors, Makro, and direct importers from Italy.
- Negotiate volume pricing and a stable supply of key items (prosciutto, provolone).
- Flour: Italian "00" or type 550/750 Polish flours. Local suppliers lower costs.

---

## 9. Marketing

- Instagram and TikTok (bread baking and slicing videos perform well).
- Google Maps listing and Pyszne/Wolt/Uber Eats (later).
- Weekly presence at fixed locations, such as business parks, Hala Koszyki area events, and food truck festivals.
- Pre-orders for offices and catering.

---

## 10. Risks

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Weather and winter seasonality | Indoor events, catering, delivery, and a heated truck |
| Expensive imported ingredients | Fixed prices, a limited menu, and mix local and Italian products |
| Location restrictions | Contracts with private landowners and event organizers |
| Permit delays | Start paperwork early |
| Operator burnout | Hire staff early and standardize recipes |

---

1. **Month 0-1:** Register the business, set up HACCP, and find a commissary kitchen. Develop recipes.
2. **Month 1-3:** Test with a pop-up (Option D) at markets and events, about 10,000-25,000 PLN.
3. **Month 3-6:** If sales hold (50+ sandwiches/day), buy a used truck or trailer (Option A).
4. **Month 12+:** Consider your own production kitchen (Option C) and a second location.

| A: Used truck, off-site baking | ~105,000-225,000 |
| C: Own kitchen and trailer | ~130,000-325,000 |

query: System analysis by David Easton
reference:
# David Easton's Systems Analysis

## Overview
David Easton (1917–2014), a Canadian-American political scientist, introduced **systems analysis** to political science, most notably in *The Political System* (1953) and *A Framework for Political Analysis* (1965) and *A Systems Analysis of Political Life* (1965). He sought a general theory to move the discipline beyond descriptive, institutional studies toward an empirical, behavioral, and theoretical science of politics.

## Core Definition
Easton defined politics as **"the authoritative allocation of values for a society."** The political system is the set of interactions through which these binding allocations are made and accepted.

## Key Concepts

1. **Political system**: A set of interactions, abstracted from total social behavior, through which values are authoritatively allocated.
2. **Environment**: Everything outside the system's boundary.
   - *Intra-societal*: economy, culture, social structure, personality
   - *Extra-societal*: international system, global ecology, other societies
3. **Inputs**
   - **Demands**: claims on the system for allocations (e.g., for jobs, education, rights)
   - **Supports**: resources and attitudes that sustain the system (obedience, taxes, voting, loyalty)
4. **Conversion (black box)**: The processes inside the system (decision-making, institutions) that transform inputs into outputs.
5. **Outputs**: Authoritative decisions, policies, and actions.
6. **Feedback loop**: Outputs shape the environment, which produces new inputs, making the process continuous and cyclical.

## Demands and Supports in Detail
- **Demand stress** can come from overload (volume) or content (complexity). The system manages this through **gatekeepers** (e.g., parties, interest groups) and by reducing or regulating demands.
- **Supports** are directed at three objects:
  - *Political community* (the group of people)
  - *Regime* (rules, values, structures)
  - *Authorities* (the office-holders)
- **Diffuse support**: deep, generalized goodwill/legitimacy that endures despite poor outputs.
- **Specific support**: tied to satisfaction with particular policies.

## Persistence and Stability
Easton focused on how systems **persist** amid stress, through:
- Responsive outputs
- Cultivating legitimacy and socialization
- Structural adjustments
- Use of coercion where necessary

## Strengths
- Provides a general, universal framework for comparing systems
- Emphasizes interdependence and dynamic processes
- Highlights the role of the environment and feedback
- Encourages empirical, interdisciplinary research

## Criticisms
- **Static/conservative bias**: emphasizes equilibrium and persistence, so it explains change poorly
- **"Black box" vagueness**: says little about internal decision-making
- **Too abstract**: hard to operationalize and test
- **Neglects power, conflict, and class**: critics, including Marxists, argue it ignores inequality
- **Ethnocentrism**: derived largely from Western (American) liberal-democratic experience
- Difficult to define system boundaries
- Easton himself later acknowledged the limits of behavioralism (his "post-behavioral revolution" in 1969).

## Simple Model

```
ENVIRONMENT
   │
 Demands + Supports (Inputs)
   ▼
[ POLITICAL SYSTEM: conversion ]
   ▼
 Decisions & Policies (Outputs)
   ▼
ENVIRONMENT ──► Feedback ──► back to Inputs
```

Would you like a shorter exam-style answer, a diagram, or a comparison with other approaches (e.g., Almond's structural-functionalism)?

System analysis refers to the study of political systems and their components, such as institutions, actors, and processes, in order to understand how they function and interact with each other. Easton's system analysis framework is based on the idea that political systems can be understood as a set of inputs, conversion processes, and outputs. Inputs refer to the demands, support, and resources that are brought into the political system by various actors and groups. Conversion processes involve the transformation of these inputs into policy decisions and actions by political institutions and actors. Finally, outputs are the outcomes and consequences of these policy decisions and actions. It has helped researchers and analysts to gain insights into the complexities of politics and to develop theories and models for explaining political behavior and outcomes.

It prompts students to reflect on issues related to health with an interdisciplinary lens and think about how they can make an impact now and in the future. HHV is not intended to purely be a stepping stone to medical school or graduate school. However, some students state that they are in HHV because it will look good on their resume. In addition, many students express frustration with the assignments in HNRS 250 and do not understand how the readings and reflections connect to their journey in the minor. Another challenge is that sometimes students may conform to the values expressed by Dr. Braitberg or other professors rather than articulating their own opinion. We suggest that HHV make changes that prompt students to develop personal connections to their work in the minor. One change to foster personal connections is to integrate group values into HHV starting in the HNRS 250 class. Group values are a set of beliefs held by a group of people that inform their actions as they work together. reference:
The Health and Human Values (HHV) minor exists to help students grow as individuals who will pursue careers in health and health care. Through an interdisciplinary lens, it asks students to reflect on the social, ethical, cultural, political, and structural forces that shape health, and to consider how they can make a difference now and in the future. Yet as mentors and former students in the program, we have seen gaps between this purpose and students' day-to-day experience. Some students treat HHV as a résumé line or a stepping stone to graduate school. Others feel frustrated by assignments that seem disconnected from their goals, overwhelmed by repetitive class formats, or uncertain about what to expect from one cohort to the next. Many also report limited opportunities to connect with students in other cohorts, alumni, or the wider Honors College.

This essay presents four change proposals intended to strengthen engagement and deepen the value of the minor. First, we recommend fostering personal connections to HHV by building group values and group agreements into HNRS 250. Second, we propose creating more experiential learning opportunities, such as guest speakers, service learning, and field trips, so that students can see how course content applies in real communities. Third, we suggest improving the organization and structure of HHV classes through consistent syllabi, shared course frameworks, and targeted feedback surveys. Finally, we propose increasing inter-cohort and alumni support through social events, peer preceptorships, an internship presentation database, an alumni directory, and collaboration with other Honors minors. Together, these changes aim to make HHV more meaningful, cohesive, and supportive for every student.
