query: Traduci in italiano "The ringing of the phone startles her so much she jumps. She’s standing next to her bed, and the phone is on the bedside table. The second ring is like a scream in the silent house. She reaches for it at once, on instinct. It could be Fred. It could be Harge. Carol doesn’t dare awake suspicion by letting it ring a third time. But when she brings the phone to her ear, the obligatory hello catches in her throat, as she remembers: Harge is at a dinner with clients; Fred is away in the Poconos with his wife for the weekend. Abby is on a date with her redhead. Which means the only possible person who could be calling her is— “Hello?” That voice, soft, almost a whisper, goes through her like a javelin. Carol’s eyes flutter shut. What she feels is the most terrible, heartbreaking, exquisite rush. The sound of Therese is like water poured down a parched throat, and like nails driven into a coffin— “Carol?” Carol’s other hand comes up, cupping the receiver as if it were Therese’s face, as if she could draw her close to her. Her heart beats a frenetic rhythm of yes and don’t and please— Her thoughts fly to last week, when Abby came out to see her for the first time. They weren’t supposed to have contact, and for all Carol knew there was still a detective watching her. But Abby had been back for over a week and Carol was starved for the sight of her, for any news she might carry. Abby came in a cab. She entered the house through the backdoor. The first thing she did was walk to the living room telephone and show Carol how to unscrew the cap on the receiver. Carol had watched in mounting confusion as Abby looked into the network of wires and breathed a sigh. “Good,” she’d said. “There’s no recording device.” Carol had thought she was past being horrified by what Harge might do, but as Abby explained to her what to look for, and that she should look for it every time she came home, fresh despair woke in her. How Abby knew about such things was just another of the inexplicable talents her friend wielded—and an insight not to be ignored. “What if I find it—the—device?” Carol asked, her voice weak. Abby pursed her lips in serious thought, and said, “If you remove it, and Harge finds out, he’ll think you’re trying to hide something from him. You’ll have to just leave it there, and know. But for now, you can call me whenever you need. Keep your eyes open for things out of place. Funny looking wires, holes in the walls. I don’t think he’d go beyond something in the phone, since really, he only wants to make sure you’re not talking to anyone but him. Still. It’s worth being cautious.” And Carol, though it makes her sick every time, has followed Abby’s directive. So far, no recording device in the phone. Which means that right now, no one but her can hear Therese’s voice, the achingly beautiful way that she says Carol’s name, the depth of the silence that rises between them. Still— ‘Not safe,’ her thoughts hiss. ‘You can’t,’ and ‘Hang up!’ She tries to do just that. But it’s like her fingers and the switch hook on the telephone are each the northern poll of a magnet, pushing against each other, resisting. Her heart hammers and her lungs seize, and she has to, she has to hang up— “Are you there?” Therese asks. ‘Hang up. Hang up!’ “If it’s not you, please just tell me…” The words send fresh agony through her, because she knows what Therese must be thinking, wondering, dreading: who is on the line? Who is listening in? What fresh violation has she laid herself open to? It’s too cruel. She can’t let her think— “It’s me,” Carol whispers. She can’t say anything else. Even if she wanted to, her throat closes in a sudden wash of terror. What is she doing? ‘Hang up!’ But she can’t. The answering silence is so complete, she could almost think that she imagined Therese was ever there. Or that the ringing in her own ears has prevented her hearing the sound of a lost call. She strains for something, anything, even the whisper of Therese’s breath. She imagines Therese’s face; pictures her standing in the hallway of her building. What wouldn’t Carol give, to have her in front of her right now, to look into her beautiful eyes, to touch her? But that thought makes fresh misery well up. She knows exactly what she wouldn’t give. What she’s choosing not to give. And what she’s giving up instead. “Are you all right?” asks Therese. Carol nearly weeps at the question. ‘All right? No, Angel. No, I’m not all right. I am wretched without you. I am miserable with my choice—and I can’t unchoose it.’ “I—” she tries to speak, but breaks off. Therese sounds hoarse, exhausted. Who knows what the past three weeks have been like for her? As bad as Carol’s? Worse? Abby was… tactful, when Carol asked about their drive back from Illinois. She clearly didn’t want Carol to feel worse than she already did (though Carol suspects that Abby is angry at her, for what she involved her in—the heartlessness and cowardice of her flight from the Drake), but Carol read easily between the lines. Therese did not take her disappearance well. Therese seems to realize that she won’t answer the question, because in that same quiet, weary voice she says, “Abby gave me your letter.” The letter. Written hastily in the early hours of the morning, while Therese slept. Carol hardly remembers what she said, only that it was torture to write. Torture, to slip out of Therese’s arms, to dress, to gather her things— “Do you remember, when I asked you… if you felt safe with me?” Carol swallows at the question, tears gathering hot in her eyes. Therese says, “You didn’t answer me. Not really. But I know now that you… that that’s why you left me. Because you’re frightened. I… understand, Carol, do you see?” Carol covers her mouth with her hand, afraid of the sob that will break out of her if she doesn’t. “I just,” Therese’s beautiful voice strains. “I just wish that you had… that you had felt safe with me, Carol. Safe enough to say goodbye. To let me say goodbye.” She does sob, then—strangling the sound behind her fist, the tears dripping down over her own fingers. If only Therese knew that those days in her company, those nights in her arms, were the safest Carol has felt in years. Oh, she wants to speak! But all her will has shattered. If she speaks, she’ll beg. Beg Therese to forgive her. Beg her to come to the house, or let her come to Therese’s apartment. In this moment she is ready to throw everything away for one more night with Therese, one more night to worship at the altar of her body—but she can’t she can’t she can’t— “You said I would understand some day. I already understand, Carol. It’s not about resolution. I need you—I need you to know, that I understand. But I—I want to… Ask you… something.” ‘I want to ask you things,’ Therese had whispered, so early on. How like that moment this one was. Therese innocent, wounded. Carol guilty, ashamed. And now, as then, she has to answer her. She owes it to her—this girl who brought the sunlight into her life, whose absence has made everything dark—to answer. “Ask me,” she says, her voice a tremulous whisper. Therese breathes in, and Carol can hear the banked sob in it, before she says with surprising steadiness, “You said I should imagine you there to greet me. I need you to tell me—I—need to know—if I’m—” she falters, breathes in, says, “if it’s just imagination. You—greeting me… again.” Carol’s eyes close, the words of her letter coming back to her in all their damning inconsistency: ‘Until then, there must be no contact between us. I have much to do—’ Yes, she does have much to do. So much, in fact, that she fears it will never end. That the sunrise will never come. Why did she dangle that carrot before her sweet Therese? What weakness drove her to it? She is only at the beginning of this trial with Harge, of the negotiations, of the careful moves, of the doctor’s appointments. The custody hearing is two months away and who knows what she will have to do in that time? She is determined to do it. Determined to do whatever she must. She won’t lose her daughter. She won’t lose Rindy. There is only one way to answer Therese: ‘I release you. I release you.’ Any other answer would be cruel, would be selfish, and she has already proved her immeasurable selfishness to this girl. Therese doesn’t deserve it. This is why she fled in the night. Because she’s not only selfish, she’s a coward, and she couldn’t bear to say the words to Therese. The words she must say. And yet before she can, visions and sensations and sounds flood her mind— That first meeting: ‘I wonder if you might help me find this doll for my daughter?’ And their first phone call: ‘Do you get a lunch hour there? Let me take you to lunch.’ Their first date: ‘Therese Belivet. It’s lovely.’ And their first, exquisite kiss. Tender. Tentative. Bending toward her with a confidence she didn’t feel, clutching her hand and cradling the back of her head and kissing her. Kissing her soft and deep and longing and hungry and feeling her kiss back— ‘Take me to bed’ — ‘You’re trembling’ — ‘No, don’t I want to see you’— ‘I want to see you I want to see you I want to see you…’ “My angel,” Carol whispers, unable to hide her tears. Unable to say what she must. “I—hope not. Darling, I hope not.” ‘Selfish selfish selfish.’ Therese says nothing for long moments. In a fever of longing and fear and hope—yes, hope —Carol wonders again if she has imagined all of this. Then she hears it. Like a benediction. “I miss you,” Therese whispers. The line disconnects. Carol stays where she is, hunched over the phone, cradling it to her ear. As if, gripping tight enough, she will be able to send her own words back across the line, fling them through space, into the heart of her love— “I miss you, too.”"

L'altra mano di Carol si alza a coppa attorno alla cornetta, come se fosse il volto di Therese, come se potesse avvicinarla a sé. Il suo cuore batte un ritmo frenetico di sì e non e per favore— I suoi pensieri volano alla settimana scorsa, quando Abby è venuta a trovarla per la prima volta. Non avrebbero dovuto avere contatto, e per quanto ne sapeva Carol c'era ancora un detective che la osservava. Ma Abby era tornata da oltre una settimana e Carol era affamata di vederla, di qualsiasi notizia potesse portare. Abby è arrivata in taxi. È entrata in casa dalla porta di servizio. La prima cosa che ha fatto è stata andare al telefono del soggiorno e mostrare a Carol come svitare il cappuccio dal ricevitore. Carol l'aveva guardata con crescente confusione mentre Abby ispezionava la rete di fili e tirava un sospiro di sollievo. "Bene," aveva detto. "Non c'è alcun dispositivo di registrazione." Carol pensava di essere al di là dell'essere orripilata da quello che Harge avrebbe potuto fare, ma mentre Abby le spiegava cosa cercare e che avrebbe dovuto farlo ogni volta che tornava a casa, in lei si è risvegliata una disperazione. Come Abby sapesse di queste cose era solo un altro dei talenti inspiegabili che la sua amica brandiva—e un'intuizione da non ignorare. "E se lo trovo—il—dispositivo?" aveva chiesto Carol, la voce debole. Abby aveva stretto le labbra in un pensiero serio e aveva detto: "Se lo rimuovi e Harge lo scopre, penserà che stai cercando di nascondergli qualcosa. Dovrai lasciarlo lì e saperlo. Ma per ora, puoi chiamarmi quando hai bisogno. Tieni gli occhi aperti per cose fuori posto. Filo strani, buchi nei muri. Ciò significa che in questo momento, nessun altro oltre a lei può sentire la voce di Therese, il modo dolorosamente bello in cui dice il nome di Carol, la profondità del silenzio che sorge tra di loro. Ancora— 'Non sicuro,' sibilano i suoi pensieri. 'Non puoi,' e 'Riattacca!' Prova proprio a fare quello. Ma è come se le sue dita e il gancio del ricevitore fossero ciascuno il polo nord di un magnete, che si spingono l'uno contro l'altro, resistendo. Il suo cuore martella e i polmoni si bloccano e lei deve, deve riattaccare— "Sei lì?" chiede Therese. 'Riattacca. Riattacca!' "Se non sei tu, per favore dimmelo..." Le parole le mandano una nuova agonia perché sa cosa deve star pensando, chiedendosi, temendo Therese: chi c'è in linea? Chi sta ascoltando? A quale nuova violazione si è esposta? È troppo crudele. Non può lasciarla pensare— "Sono io," sussurra Carol. Non riesce a dire altro. Anche se volesse, la gola si chiude in un'improvvisa ondata di terrore. Cosa sta facendo? 'Riattacca!' Ma non riesce. Il silenzio che risponde è così completo che potrebbe quasi pensare di essersi immaginata che Therese ci fosse mai stata. O che il fischio nelle proprie orecchie le abbia impedito di sentire il suono di una chiamata persa. Si sforza di cercare qualcosa, qualsiasi cosa, anche il respiro di Therese. Immagina il volto di Therese; la immagina in piedi nel corridoio del suo palazzo. Quanto vorrebbe Carol averla di fronte in questo momento, per guardare nei suoi bellissimi occhi, per toccarla? Ma quel pensiero fa sorgere una miseria nuova. Sa esattamente cosa non darebbe. Quello che sta scegliendo di non dare. E ciò che sta abbandonando invece. "Stai bene?" chiede Therese. Carol quasi piange per la domanda. 'Bene? No, angelo. No, non sto bene. Sono misera senza di te. Sono infelice per la mia scelta—e non posso cambiarla.' "Io—" prova a parlare, ma si interrompe. Therese suona rauca, esausta. Chissà com'erano state le ultime tre settimane per lei. Peggio di quanto fossero per Carol? Peggio? Abby è stata... discreta, quando Carol ha chiesto del loro viaggio di ritorno dall'Illinois. Chiaramente non voleva che Carol si sentisse peggio di quanto già non si sentisse (anche se Carol sospetta che Abby sia arrabbiata con lei, per quello che l'ha coinvolta in—l'insensibilità e la codardia della sua fuga dal Drake), ma Carol legge facilmente tra le righe. Therese non ha preso bene la sua scomparsa. Therese sembra capire che non risponderà alla domanda, perché con quella stessa voce tranquilla e stanca dice: "Abby mi ha dato la tua lettera." La lettera. Scritta frettolosamente nelle prime ore del mattino, mentre Therese dormiva. Carol a malapena ricorda cosa ha detto, solo che è stato un tormento scriverla. Un tormento, uscire dalle braccia di Therese, vestirsi, raccogliere le sue cose— "Ti ricordi, quando ti ho chiesto... se ti sentivi al sicuro con me?" Carol deglutisce alla domanda, le lacrime calde si raccolgono nei suoi occhi. Therese dice: "Non mi hai risposto. Non veramente. Ma ora so che tu... che per quello mi hai lasciato. Perché hai paura. "Volevo solo che tu avessi... che tu ti fossi sentita al sicuro con me, Carol. Abbastanza al sicuro per dire addio. Per lasciarmi dire addio." Se solo Therese sapesse che quei giorni in sua compagnia, quelle notti tra le sue braccia, erano i più sicuri che Carol avesse sentito in anni. Oh, vuole parlare! Ma tutta la sua volontà si è frantumata. Se parla, implorerà. Implorerà Therese di perdonarla. Di venire a casa, o di lasciarla andare nell'appartamento di Therese. In questo momento è pronta a gettare via tutto per un'altra notte con Therese, un'altra notte per adorarla al santuario del suo corpo—ma non può non può non può— "Mi hai detto che un giorno avrei capito. Io capisco già, Carol. Non si tratta di risoluzione. Ho bisogno che tu sappia—che io capisco. Ma io—voglio... Chiederti... qualcosa." 'Voglio chiederti delle cose,' Therese aveva sussurrato, tanto tempo fa. Com'è simile questo momento a quello. Therese innocente, ferita. Carol colpevole, imbarazzata. E ora, come allora, deve risponderle. Le deve—questa ragazza che ha portato il sole nella sua vita, la cui assenza ha reso tutto scuro—rispondere. "Chiedimi," dice lei, la voce un tremulo sussurro. Therese inspira, e Carol può sentire il singhiozzo trattenuto, prima che con sorprendente fermezza dica: "Mi hai detto che dovrei immaginarti lì ad accogliermi. Ho bisogno che mi dica—ho—bisogno di sapere—se sono—" vacilla, inspira, dice, "se è solo immaginazione. Tu—che mi accogli... di nuovo." Gli occhi di Carol si chiudono, le parole della sua lettera le tornano alla mente con tutta la loro dannata incoerenza: 'Fino ad allora, non deve esserci contatto tra noi. Ho molto da fare—' Sì, ha molto da fare. Talmente tanto, infatti, che teme che non finirà mai. Che l'alba non arriverà mai. Perché ha fatto quella promessa alla sua dolce Therese? Che debolezza la spingeva? È solo all’inizio di questo processo con Harge, delle negoziazioni, delle mosse caute, degli appuntamenti dal dottore. L'udienza per l'affidamento è tra due mesi e chi sa cosa dovrà fare in quel tempo? È determinata a farlo. Determinata a fare tutto ciò che deve. Non perderà sua figlia. Non perderà Rindy. C'è solo un modo per rispondere a Therese: 'Ti lascio andare. Ti lascio andare.' Ogni altra risposta sarebbe crudele, sarebbe egoista, e lei ha già dimostrato la sua inimmaginabile egoismo a questa ragazza. Therese non lo merita. È per questo che è fuggita nella notte. Perché non solo è egoista, è una codarda, e non poteva sopportare di dire quelle parole a Therese. Le parole che deve dire. Eppure prima che possa, visioni e sensazioni e suoni invadono la sua mente— Quel primo incontro: 'Mi chiedo se potresti aiutarmi a trovare questa bambola per mia figlia?' E la loro prima chiamata telefonica: 'Hai un'ora di pausa lì? Lascia che ti porti a pranzo.' Il loro primo appuntamento: 'Therese Belivet. È adorabile.' E il loro primo, squisito bacio. Tenere. Titubante. Accostarsi a lei con una fiducia che non sentiva, stringendo la sua mano e accogliendo la parte posteriore della sua testa e baciarla. Baciarla dolcemente e profondamente e desiderosamente e affamata e sentendo lei rispondere al bacio— 'Portami a letto' — 'Stai tremando' — 'No, non voglio vederti'— 'Voglio vederti voglio vederti voglio vederti...' "Mio angelo," sussurra Carol, incapace di nascondere le lacrime. Incapace di dire quello che deve. "Io—spero di no. Amore, spero di no." 'Egoista egoista egoista.' Therese non dice nulla per lunghi momenti. In un febbre di desiderio e paura e speranza—sì, speranza—Carol si chiede di nuovo se abbia immaginato tutto questo. Poi lo sente. Come una benedizione. "Mi manchi," sussurra Therese. La linea si disconnette. Carol rimane dov'è, accovacciata sopra il telefono, stringendolo all'orecchio. Come se, aggrappandosi abbastanza forte, sarà in grado di mandare indietro le sue parole lungo la linea, lanciarle attraverso lo spazio, nel cuore del suo amore— "Anche tu mi manchi."

meta.redacted_query: "The ringing of the phone startles her so much she jumps. She’s standing next to her bed, and the phone is on the bedside table. The second ring is like a scream in the silent house. She reaches for it at once, on instinct. It could be Fred. It could be [REDACTED]. Carol doesn’t dare awake suspicion by letting it ring a third time. But when she brings the phone to her ear, the obligatory hello catches in her throat, as she remembers: [REDACTED] is at a dinner with clients; Fred is away in the [REDACTED] with his wife for the weekend. Abby is on a date with her redhead. Which means the only possible person who could be calling her is— “Hello?” That voice, soft, almost a whisper, goes through her like a javelin. Carol’s eyes flutter shut. What she feels is the most terrible, heartbreaking, exquisite rush. The sound of Therese is like water poured down a parched throat, and like nails driven into a coffin— “Carol?” Carol’s other hand comes up, cupping the receiver as if it were Therese’s face, as if she could draw her close to her. Her heart beats a frenetic rhythm of yes and don’t and please— Her thoughts fly to last week, when Abby came out to see her for the first time. They weren’t supposed to have contact, and for all Carol knew there was still a detective watching her. But Abby had been back for over a week and Carol was starved for the sight of her, for any news she might carry. Abby came in a cab. She entered the house through the backdoor. The first thing she did was walk to the living room telephone and show Carol how to unscrew the cap on the receiver. Carol had watched in mounting confusion as Abby looked into the network of wires and breathed a sigh. “Good,” she’d said. “There’s no recording device.” Carol had thought she was past being horrified by what [REDACTED] might do, but as Abby explained to her what to look for, and that she should look for it every time she came home, fresh despair woke in her. How Abby knew about such things was just another of the inexplicable talents her friend wielded—and an insight not to be ignored. “What if I find it—the—device?” Carol asked, her voice weak. Abby pursed her lips in serious thought, and said, “If you remove it, and [REDACTED] finds out, he’ll think you’re trying to hide something from him. You’ll have to just leave it there, and know. But for now, you can call me whenever you need. Keep your eyes open for things out of place. Funny looking wires, holes in the walls. I don’t think he’d go beyond something in the phone, since really, he only wants to make sure you’re not talking to anyone but him. Still. It’s worth being cautious.” And Carol, though it makes her sick every time, has followed Abby’s directive. So far, no recording device in the phone. Which means that right now, no one but her can hear Therese’s voice, the achingly beautiful way that she says Carol’s name, the depth of the silence that rises between them. Still— ‘Not safe,’ her thoughts hiss. ‘You can’t,’ and ‘Hang up!’ She tries to do just that. But it’s like her fingers and the switch hook on the telephone are each the northern poll of a magnet, pushing against each other, resisting. Her heart hammers and her lungs seize, and she has to, she has to hang up— “Are you there?” Therese asks. ‘Hang up. Hang up!’ “If it’s not you, please just tell me…” The words send fresh agony through her, because she knows what Therese must be thinking, wondering, dreading: who is on the line? Who is listening in? What fresh violation has she laid herself open to? It’s too cruel. She can’t let her think— “It’s me,” Carol whispers. She can’t say anything else. Even if she wanted to, her throat closes in a sudden wash of terror. What is she doing? ‘Hang up!’ But she can’t. The answering silence is so complete, she could almost think that she imagined Therese was ever there. Or that the ringing in her own ears has prevented her hearing the sound of a lost call. She strains for something, anything, even the whisper of Therese’s breath. She imagines Therese’s face; pictures her standing in the hallway of her building. What wouldn’t Carol give, to have her in front of her right now, to look into her beautiful eyes, to touch her? But that thought makes fresh misery well up. She knows exactly what she wouldn’t give. What she’s choosing not to give. And what she’s giving up instead. “Are you all right?” asks Therese. Carol nearly weeps at the question. ‘All right? No, Angel. No, I’m not all right. I am wretched without you. I am miserable with my choice—and I can’t unchoose it.’ “I—” she tries to speak, but breaks off. Therese sounds hoarse, exhausted. Who knows what the past three weeks have been like for her? As bad as Carol’s? Worse? Abby was… tactful, when Carol asked about their drive back from [REDACTED]. She clearly didn’t want Carol to feel worse than she already did (though Carol suspects that Abby is angry at her, for what she involved her in—the heartlessness and cowardice of her flight from the [REDACTED]), but Carol read easily between the lines. Therese did not take her disappearance well. Therese seems to realize that she won’t answer the question, because in that same quiet, weary voice she says, “Abby gave me your letter.” The letter. Written hastily in the early hours of the morning, while Therese slept. Carol hardly remembers what she said, only that it was torture to write. Torture, to slip out of Therese’s arms, to dress, to gather her things— “Do you remember, when I asked you… if you felt safe with me?” Carol swallows at the question, tears gathering hot in her eyes. Therese says, “You didn’t answer me. Not really. But I know now that you… that that’s why you left me. Because you’re frightened. I… understand, Carol, do you see?” Carol covers her mouth with her hand, afraid of the sob that will break out of her if she doesn’t. “I just,” Therese’s beautiful voice strains. “I just wish that you had… that you had felt safe with me, Carol. Safe enough to say goodbye. To let me say goodbye.” She does sob, then—strangling the sound behind her fist, the tears dripping down over her own fingers. If only Therese knew that those days in her company, those nights in her arms, were the safest Carol has felt in years. Oh, she wants to speak! But all her will has shattered. If she speaks, she’ll beg. Beg Therese to forgive her. Beg her to come to the house, or let her come to Therese’s apartment. In this moment she is ready to throw everything away for one more night with Therese, one more night to worship at the altar of her body—but she can’t she can’t she can’t— “You said I would understand some day. I already understand, Carol. It’s not about resolution. I need you—I need you to know, that I understand. But I—I want to… Ask you… something.” ‘I want to ask you things,’ Therese had whispered, so early on. How like that moment this one was. Therese innocent, wounded. Carol guilty, ashamed. And now, as then, she has to answer her. She owes it to her—this girl who brought the sunlight into her life, whose absence has made everything dark—to answer. “Ask me,” she says, her voice a tremulous whisper. Therese breathes in, and Carol can hear the banked sob in it, before she says with surprising steadiness, “You said I should imagine you there to greet me. I need you to tell me—I—need to know—if I’m—” she falters, breathes in, says, “if it’s just imagination. You—greeting me… again.” Carol’s eyes close, the words of her letter coming back to her in all their damning inconsistency: ‘Until then, there must be no contact between us. I have much to do—’ Yes, she does have much to do. So much, in fact, that she fears it will never end. That the sunrise will never come. Why did she dangle that carrot before her sweet Therese? What weakness drove her to it? She is only at the beginning of this trial with [REDACTED], of the negotiations, of the careful moves, of the doctor’s appointments. The custody hearing is two months away and who knows what she will have to do in that time? She is determined to do it. Determined to do whatever she must. She won’t lose her daughter. She won’t lose [REDACTED]. There is only one way to answer Therese: ‘I release you. I release you.’ Any other answer would be cruel, would be selfish, and she has already proved her immeasurable selfishness to this girl. Therese doesn’t deserve it. This is why she fled in the night. Because she's not only selfish, she's a coward, and she couldn’t bear to say the words to Therese. The words she must say. And yet before she can, visions and sensations and sounds flood her mind— That first meeting: ‘I wonder if you might help me find this doll for my daughter?’ And their first phone call: ‘Do you get a lunch hour there? Let me take you to lunch.’ Their first date: ‘[REDACTED]. It’s lovely.’ And their first, exquisite kiss. Tender. Tentative. Bending toward her with a confidence she didn’t feel, clutching her hand and cradling the back of her head and kissing her. Kissing her soft and deep and longing and hungry and feeling her kiss back— ‘Take me to bed’ — ‘You’re trembling’ — ‘No, don’t I want to see you’— ‘I want to see you I want to see you I want to see you…’ “My angel,” Carol whispers, unable to hide her tears. Unable to say what she must. “I—hope not. Darling, I hope not.” ‘Selfish selfish selfish.’ Therese says nothing for long moments. In a fever of longing and fear and hope—yes, hope —Carol wonders again if she has imagined all of this. Then she hears it. Like a benediction. “I miss you,” Therese whispers. The line disconnects. Carol stays where she is, hunched over the phone, cradling it to her ear. As if, gripping tight enough, she will be able to send her own words back across the line, fling them through space, into the heart of her love— “I miss you, too.”"

# Quiz No. 3: Percent by Mass ↔ Molarity

## Part 1: My own parallel problem

**Problem:** A sulfuric acid solution is 40.0% H₂SO₄ by mass and has a density of 1.30 g/mL. What is its molarity?

**Step 1: Assume 100.0 g of solution.**

**Step 2: Mass of solute.**
mass H₂SO₄ = (40.0 / 100) × 100.0 g = 40.0 g

**Step 3: Moles of solute** (molar mass H₂SO₄ = 98.08 g/mol).
40.0 g ÷ 98.08 g/mol = 0.408 mol H₂SO₄

**Step 4: Liters of solution** (from the density).
100.0 g × (1 mL / 1.30 g) = 76.9 mL = 0.0769 L

query: Yasmin frequently hypnotizes her willing & docile friend Dave. In this script, Yasmin has arranged to 'lend' Dave to her overweight friend Morag for the day. He's going to do all her housework for her, and *anything* else she Morag tells him to do.
reference:
# **On Loan**

*A comedy-drama scene in one act*

---

**INT. YASMIN'S FLAT – SATURDAY MORNING**

*Dave sits upright on the sofa, hands on his knees, eyes glazed and peaceful. YASMIN stands beside him, holding a mug of tea. MORAG, mid-forties, cheerful, in a comfortable cardigan, hovers by the door holding a tote bag.*

**MORAG:** Is he... is he actually under?

**YASMIN:** Deep as a well. *(snaps her fingers near his ear; Dave doesn't flinch)* Dave, what are you?

**DAVE:** *(slow, dreamy)* Relaxed. Obedient. Ready to help.

**MORAG:** *(delighted whisper)* Oh, that's *brilliant*.

**YASMIN:** Right, ground rules, Morag. I've already set them with Dave while he was awake, so he knows what he's agreed to. He'll do housework, errands, cooking, lifting, anything practical. Nothing dangerous, nothing humiliating in front of other people, nothing illegal, and nothing that Dave wouldn't be happy to do awake. If he's uncomfortable, he'll surface by himself.

**MORAG:** Fair enough. And if *I* need him to stop?

**YASMIN:** Say "Dave, sleep and settle," and he'll go calm and still. To wake him fully, say "Dave, clear and bright." Both work for you. *(to Dave)* Dave, for the rest of today, you'll listen to Morag as you listen to me. You'll take pride in doing things well. When I count to three, you'll open your eyes, still deeply relaxed, and ready to start. One... two... three.

*Dave's eyes open. He stands smoothly and faces Morag with a pleasant, blank smile.*

**DAVE:** Good morning, Morag. How can I help?

**MORAG:** *(to Yasmin, thrilled)* Oh, I could cry. Have you *seen* my kitchen?

**YASMIN:** I have. Good luck, Dave. *(grabbing her coat)* I'll collect him at six. Don't let her work you too hard.

**DAVE:** *(serenely)* I'll do my best.

---

**INT. MORAG'S HOUSE – KITCHEN – LATER**

*A heroic pile of dishes. Dave, in rubber gloves and an apron that says KISS THE COOK, scrubs with calm precision. Morag sits at the table with a cup of tea and a notepad.*

**MORAG:** Right. After the dishes: the hob, the oven, and the fridge. Then hoovering upstairs, then the bathroom...

**DAVE:** Yes, Morag.

**MORAG:** *(muttering, writing)* I could get used to this. *(louder)* Dave, when you've finished the fridge, could you sort the Tupperware cupboard? The lids never match.

**DAVE:** Matching the lids. Of course.

**MORAG:** *(a little guiltily)* You can say no, you know.

**DAVE:** *(dreamy smile)* I don't want to say no. It feels nice to be useful.

---

**INT. MORAG'S HOUSE – LIVING ROOM – AFTERNOON**

*Dave is up a stepladder, dusting the top of a bookshelf. Morag is on the sofa, feet up, with a magazine.*

**MORAG:** Dave, while you're up there, could you change the lightbulb in the hall? And then bring me a biscuit? Actually, two biscuits.

**DAVE:** Lightbulb, then biscuits. Two.

**MORAG:** *(to herself)* And the garden. And the windows. And that wardrobe I keep meaning to clear out...

*She pauses and looks at him, a little thoughtful.*

**MORAG:** Dave, can I ask you something odd? Do you actually enjoy this?

**DAVE:** *(climbing down, considering)* It's very peaceful. There's nothing to worry about. Just one task, then the next.

**MORAG:** *(softly)* Hm. Sounds lovely, honestly.

---

**INT. MORAG'S HOUSE – KITCHEN – EVENING**

*Everything gleams. A casserole is in the oven. Morag has laid out two plates. Dave stands at the counter, hands folded.*

**MORAG:** Dave, you've been marvellous. Sit down. That's an instruction.

**DAVE:** *(sitting)* Yes, Morag.

**MORAG:** Eat with me. And relax. That's another instruction.

*Dave lets out a long, contented breath. The doorbell rings. Morag opens it to reveal YASMIN.*

**YASMIN:** Well? Did he behave?

**MORAG:** I've never had such a perfect day. I'm tempted to keep him.

**YASMIN:** *(laughing)* Rental terms are strictly twenty-four hours. *(to Dave)* Dave, clear and bright.

*Dave blinks and looks around, then at the gleaming kitchen, then at the apron.*

**DAVE:** Oh no. Did I clean the *oven*?

**MORAG:** Twice.

**DAVE:** *(grinning, to Yasmin)* Next time, I'm charging.

**MORAG:** *(handing over a foil-wrapped plate of casserole)* Payment in advance.

*They laugh. FADE OUT.*

---

reference: **Study Overview and Implications** The groundbreaking research conducted by Di Renzo et al. (2015) aimed to elucidate the reproductive health impacts of exposure to toxic environmental chemicals. The study meticulously outlined how various common environmental pollutants, such as pesticides, air pollutants, metals, and endocrine-disrupting chemicals, adversely affect the health of pregnant women, fetuses, and reproductive outcomes. One pivotal finding from this research is the discernible link between exposure to these chemicals and a range of adverse health outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and developmental defects. Expectant mothers stand as one of the primary audiences who can greatly benefit from these findings. The study not only raises awareness about the potential dangers these women face from environmental pollutants but also empowers them with knowledge, potentially guiding them in mitigating unnecessary exposures. Understanding this risk profile may encourage expectant mothers to advocate for safer environmental practices and regulations, seek out environments with better air quality, and be more vigilant about avoiding high-risk substances. Families and married couples planning for children could also utilize this information by adjusting lifestyle choices and domestic environments to foster healthier reproductive outcomes. Knowledge of toxic substances at play could transform the choices they make, influencing their residential decisions, consumer behavior, and even political engagement to support environmental reforms for safer communities. Young people exposed to stress and addictive substances are another significant group that could stand to gain knowledge from this research. Often on the cusp of their reproductive years, understanding the long-term implications of their exposure could inform better life decisions, aid in lobbying for healthier college campuses and work environments, and inspire engagement with public health initiatives that target environmental health. Healthcare professionals, as key interpreters and implementers of such research, can integrate these findings into their practice by increased screening for environmental exposures, offering advice for risk reduction, and continuing education to stay abreast of new research. They can also contribute to the broader dialogue on environmental health policy, bolstered by evidence-based understanding of these risks. **Limitations of the Study** Despite the valuable insights garnered from the study by Di Renzo et al. (2015), several limitations warrant consideration. Firstly, the global nature of this research brings variability in environmental laws, exposure levels, and health outcomes that may not apply uniformly across different populations. Hence, the transferability and applicability of the findings may require regional adaptation. Secondly, the mixed-method approaches of correlating reproductive outcomes with environmental exposures face challenges of causal inferences due to potential confounding factors. Lifestyle, genetic predispositions, and other environmental factors not wholly accounted for might skew the perceived impacts of toxic chemicals. Furthermore, the rapid evolution of manufacturing practices introduces new chemicals into environments faster than research can reliably assess their implications. This timing gap leaves practitioners and patients relying on incomplete information for making crucial health decisions. Lastly, the article targets only a slice of reproductive health, potentially overlooking broader systemic health impacts associated with environmental exposures that could also influence reproductive outcomes. **Next Steps** In light of these findings and limitations, the next logical step in research would be to conduct longitudinal and cross-sectional studies focusing on specific chemicals and their direct impact on reproductive health outcomes. These studies should prioritize establishing causal relationships and consider variables such as timing, dosage, and individual susceptibilities to exposure. Additionally, there would be value in increasing research into the effectiveness of different interventions at the personal, community, and policy levels to reduce harmful exposures. Participation in community and policy initiatives should also be investigated to understand the broader social effects. Moreover, exploring the epigenetic changes resulting from exposures and their potential to affect several generations could significantly extend the current research. Investigations into the long-term implications of these epigenetic modifications could help in developing better predictive models for individual risks. Finally, the development of advanced monitoring and diagnostic tools for early detection of environmental pollutant levels in human tissues would augment preventative approaches in healthcare and support more personalized patient guidance. **Conclusion** Di Renzo et al. (2015) have contributed significantly to the field of reproductive health and toxicology by highlighting the insidious threats posed by environmental chemicals. The implications of their study demand concerted attention from expectant mothers, families, young individuals, and healthcare professionals in forming a united front against environmental health hazards. While there are limitations to their findings, such as regional applicability and potential confounding variables, the importance of continued research in this area is unequivocal. The pursuit of deeper insights through more granular studies, interventions, and advanced technology informs the next frontier in safeguarding reproductive health against the backdrop of an increasingly polluted world. This ongoing effort not only has the potential to improve individual health outcomes but will also resonate through public policy, ultimately striving for healthier communities and environments.

query: translate text below to persian Graphite bomb (also, known as the soft bomb) is a non-lethal weapon which is used for shutting down the power supply systems of the enemy. The working mechanism of the graphite bomb is relatively simple and is based on making suspensions of air/clouds of carbon filament chemically treated extremely fine over the electrical components, causing short circuits and electrical discharges within the infrastructure of electricity supply (in especially on the power plants, transformer stations, air transportation facilities of electrical power etc.). In addition, the effective use of this unconventional electronic attack system is based on critical points identification and disruption philosophy. Carbon filaments used inside of graphite bombs are very small and may give rise to dense clouds, with a long persistence. Also, the name of soft bomb it comes from that its basic destructive eects are centered only on the electricity supply facilities, with minimal risk of occurrence of some collateral damage and particularly over the human staff [1-3].In other news, the eect of the graphite bomb is only over the equipment and facilities of uninsulated power supply. Figure 1 shows the effects of graphity bombs launched by US Air Force, on 22 March 2003 on a 400 kV Transformer Station in the Electrical Power in Nasiriyya, which caused the power shortage in the city for 30 days Graphite bomb was used against Iraq in the first Gulf War (1990-1991), neutralizing about 85% of this country facilities supply electricity. Also, the graphite bomb (composed of submunitions BLU-114/B, produced by USA) was used widely in the NATO military intervention in former Yugoslavia (1999), where its effect consisted in disabling of more than 70% national grid electricity supply Although initially in less than 24 hours, the Serbs have managed to restore their electrical systems operability, however, repeated use of the graphite bomb by alliance thwarted almost any further effort in this direction. In the final phase of this intervention, NATO air forces used mostly standard carrier vectors (e.g., bombs, missiles etc.) to transport and detonation of the munitions in the area of interest of the graphite bomb.In addition, for an accurate understanding of the multiple implications (economic, social, etc.) and respectively, the effective conditions of use in a military conflict of a graphite bomb, it is very useful a summary of the main features of a modern system of electrical energy distribution.It should be remembered first that any modern network of power supply has a high-degree of complexity and, respectively, a wide-range of distribution and therefore the decommissioning of its elements vital involves subsequently a technological eort and substantial financial for a long time. It should also be remembered that, any system of power supply will contain in its architecture the following basic elements: the generator of electricity, the electricity transmission system (incorporating in its structure the high-power transformers, losses into transmission lines which are reasonable if the line voltage is very high, typically up to 400 kV) and the electricity distribution system to the users, industrial and domestic use (i.e., this system consists mainly by the primary distribution subsystem providing voltages between 2.4 and 35 kV and respectively, secondary distribution subsystem providing voltages between 110/220 and 600 V). Theoretically, any of these sub-components may represent a potential target for an attack based on graphite bombs.In the special literature (e.g., documents prepared by NERC/North American Electric Reliability Council etc.), the concept used in the moment when a facility or electricity supply system, as a its whole, suers damage (or collapse) is called generic blackout (shutdown or blindness). In fact, the blackout is a condition which is satisfied when a significant part or the entire electrical network is damaged. Any module containing connections to the high-voltage network and that cannot support a reasonable level disturbances is a significant candidate for the blackout (and of course, for the action of graphite bombs). As it is already known, the carbon is a nonmetal chemical element in group 4, which is found in nature in two allotropic states: diamond and respectively, graphite. The graphite contains a special type of atomic network called atomic layered network which is represented by a hexagonal atomic network composed by parallel planes of carbon atoms. The hardness of the graphite is by ten times lower than of the diamond one (1 on the Mohs scale), with a density of 2.262 g/cm2. Also, the graphite is an excellent conductor of heat and power (i.e., these properties are generated by the presence into graphite of the chemical pi links, and in which the electrons are moving free between the carbon atoms through the overlapping orbits 2p) and generally, its physical properties (including its electrical conductivity) are determined by the atomic structure resulting from the specific application of some chemical treatments. Also, the graphite may not be molten and for a temperature more than 35000 0C, it directly forms the vapor carbon atoms. In addition, graphite has a low reactivity and practically, does not chemically interact with any other substance.Next, the intrinsic working mechanism of the graphite bombs action will synthetically described. Taking into account the suggestive scenario illustrated in Figure 2, the basic key-stages of its internal mechanism are the following (see Figure 3).1) The overhead of the target of interest is accomplished breaking the carrier vector (e.g., a laser-guided bombs etc.) and using a spin moving, the dispersion of the submunitions components takes place (e.g., 100 up to 200 submunitions), the size of each submunitions being by cm order;2) Each component submunitions have attached a small parachute allowing a decreasing of its fall rate, while ensuring its vertical positioning;3) A small internal explosion in each submunitions assures its breaking and respectively, releasing a coil (reel) of carbon filaments;4) The carbon filaments because of the movement of the printed coil are released and form overlapping spider webs like a network (webs);5) These carbon filament nets are highly conductive and overlapping over power lines, having as eect the voltage peaks which are overloading electrical circuits and thus, leads to deactivation of the power supply.Generally, having as starting point the strict confidentiality of the documents related to the technology used in the design and development of the graphite bombs, the access to the relevant information in this field is more dicult. Next, the filaments of carbon fiber dispersed by the BLU-114/B submunitions come into direct contact with the power transformers and other high-voltage equipments. **بمب گرافیتی: مروری بر کاربردهای نظامی اصلی آن**

بمب گرافیتی (که با نام «بمب نرم» نیز شناخته می‌شود) سلاحی غیرکشنده است که برای از کار انداختن سامانه‌های تأمین برق دشمن به کار می‌رود. سازوکار کار آن نسبتاً ساده است و بر ایجاد معلق‌هایی (ابرهایی) از رشته‌های بسیار ظریف کربنی که به‌صورت شیمیایی عمل‌آوری شده‌اند، روی اجزای الکتریکی استوار است. این رشته‌ها باعث اتصال کوتاه و تخلیه الکتریکی در زیرساخت‌های تأمین برق می‌شوند (به‌ویژه در نیروگاه‌ها، پست‌های ترانسفورماتور، تأسیسات انتقال هوایی نیروی برق و غیره). علاوه بر این، استفاده مؤثر از این سامانه حمله الکترونیکی غیرمتعارف بر فلسفه شناسایی نقاط بحرانی و مختل‌کردن آن‌ها مبتنی است. رشته‌های کربنی به‌کاررفته در بمب‌های گرافیتی بسیار کوچک‌اند و می‌توانند ابرهای متراکمی با ماندگاری طولانی ایجاد کنند. نام «بمب نرم» نیز از آن‌جا می‌آید که اثرات تخریبی اصلی آن تنها بر تأسیسات تأمین برق متمرکز است و خطر خسارات جانبی، به‌ویژه برای نیروی انسانی، حداقل است [۱-۳]. به عبارت دیگر، اثر بمب گرافیتی فقط بر تجهیزات و تأسیسات برق بدون عایق است.

شکل ۱ اثرات بمب‌های گرافیتی پرتاب‌شده توسط نیروی هوایی آمریکا در ۲۲ مارس ۲۰۰۳ بر یک پست ترانسفورماتور ۴۰۰ کیلوولت در ناصریه عراق را نشان می‌دهد که باعث کمبود برق در این شهر به مدت ۳۰ روز شد. بمب گرافیتی در جنگ اول خلیج فارس (۱۹۹۰-۱۹۹۱) علیه عراق به کار رفت و حدود ۸۵٪ از تأسیسات تأمین برق این کشور را از کار انداخت. همچنین بمب گرافیتی (متشکل از مهمات خوشه‌ای BLU-114/B ساخت آمریکا) به‌طور گسترده در مداخله نظامی ناتو در یوگسلاوی سابق (۱۹۹۹) استفاده شد و اثر آن از کار افتادن بیش از ۷۰٪ برق شبکه سراسری بود. اگرچه صرب‌ها در ابتدا ظرف کمتر از ۲۴ ساعت توانستند عملکرد سامانه‌های برق خود را بازگردانند، استفاده مکرر ائتلاف از بمب گرافیتی تقریباً هر تلاش بعدی در این جهت را ناکام گذاشت. در مرحله پایانی این مداخله، نیروهای هوایی ناتو بیشتر از حامل‌های استاندارد (مانند بمب‌ها، موشک‌ها و غیره) برای حمل و انفجار مهمات در منطقه هدف بمب گرافیتی استفاده کردند.

برای درک دقیق پیامدهای متعدد (اقتصادی، اجتماعی و غیره) و نیز شرایط مؤثر استفاده از بمب گرافیتی در یک درگیری نظامی، مرور خلاصه‌ای از ویژگی‌های اصلی یک سامانه مدرن توزیع انرژی الکتریکی بسیار مفید است. نخست باید به یاد داشت که هر شبکه مدرن تأمین برق درجه پیچیدگی بالا و گستره توزیع وسیعی دارد؛ بنابراین از کار افتادن عناصر حیاتی آن مستلزم تلاش فناورانه و هزینه مالی قابل‌توجه برای مدتی طولانی است. همچنین باید یادآور شد که هر سامانه تأمین برق در معماری خود این عناصر پایه را دارد: مولد برق، سامانه انتقال برق (شامل ترانسفورماتورهای پرقدرت؛ تلفات خطوط انتقال زمانی معقول است که ولتاژ خط بسیار بالا، معمولاً تا ۴۰۰ کیلوولت، باشد) و سامانه توزیع برق به مصرف‌کنندگان صنعتی و خانگی (این سامانه عمدتاً از زیرسامانه توزیع اولیه با ولتاژ ۲٫۴ تا ۳۵ کیلوولت و زیرسامانه توزیع ثانویه با ولتاژ ۱۱۰/۲۲۰ تا ۶۰۰ ولت تشکیل می‌شود). از نظر تئوری، هر یک از این زیرمجموعه‌ها می‌تواند هدف بالقوه حمله با بمب‌های گرافیتی باشد.

در ادبیات تخصصی (مثلاً اسناد تهیه‌شده توسط NERC/شورای قابلیت اطمینان برق آمریکای شمالی و غیره)، مفهومی که برای لحظه‌ای به کار می‌رود که یک تأسیسات یا کل سامانه تأمین برق دچار آسیب (یا فروپاشی) شود، به‌طور کلی «بلک‌اوت» (خاموشی یا کوری) نامیده می‌شود. در واقع بلک‌اوت وضعیتی است که در آن بخش قابل‌توجهی از شبکه برق یا کل آن آسیب ببیند. هر ماژولی که به شبکه فشار قوی متصل باشد و نتواند سطح معقولی از اختلالات را تحمل کند، کاندیدای مهم بلک‌اوت (و البته هدف عمل بمب‌های گرافیتی) است. علاوه بر این، در برخی اسناد نظامی بمب گرافیتی «بمب بلک‌اوت» نیز نامیده می‌شود.

به‌طور کلی وضعیت بلک‌اوت می‌تواند نتیجه بروز ناپایداری‌های دینامیکی صنعتی (مانند تغییر پارامترهای اسمی ژنراتورهای در حال کار، بروز اتصال کوتاه ناشی از اثر گرما یا شرایط جوی نامساعد و غیره) یا القای مصنوعی آن‌ها باشد. همان‌طور که پیش‌تر گفته شد، بار رزمی این بمب‌ها بر استفاده گسترده از گرافیت استوار است. چنان‌که می‌دانیم، کربن عنصری نافلز از گروه ۴ است که در طبیعت در دو شکل آلوتروپ یافت می‌شود: الماس و گرافیت. گرافیت نوع خاصی از شبکه اتمی به نام شبکه اتمی لایه‌ای دارد که با شبکه اتمی شش‌ضلعی متشکل از صفحات موازی اتم‌های کربن نشان داده می‌شود. سختی گرافیت ده برابر کمتر از الماس است (۱ در مقیاس موس) و چگالی آن ۲٫۲۶۲ گرم بر سانتی‌متر مربع [مکعب] است. همچنین گرافیت رسانای عالی گرما و برق است (این خواص ناشی از وجود پیوندهای شیمیایی پی در گرافیت است که در آن الکترون‌ها از طریق همپوشانی اوربیتال‌های 2p آزادانه بین اتم‌های کربن حرکت می‌کنند) و به‌طور کلی خواص فیزیکی آن (از جمله رسانایی الکتریکی) به ساختار اتمی حاصل از اعمال برخی عمل‌آوری‌های شیمیایی خاص بستگی دارد. همچنین گرافیت ذوب نمی‌شود و در دمای بیش از ۳۵۰۰۰ درجه سانتی‌گراد مستقیماً به اتم‌های بخار کربن تبدیل می‌شود. افزون بر این، گرافیت واکنش‌پذیری پایینی دارد و عملاً با هیچ ماده دیگری وارد برهم‌کنش شیمیایی نمی‌شود.

در ادامه، سازوکار درونی عمل بمب‌های گرافیتی به‌طور خلاصه توصیف می‌شود. با توجه به سناریوی نمایش‌داده‌شده در شکل ۲، مراحل کلیدی سازوکار داخلی آن به شرح زیر است (شکل ۳ را ببینید):

۱) بالای هدف مورد نظر، حامل (مثلاً بمب هدایت‌شونده لیزری و غیره) شکسته می‌شود و با حرکت چرخشی، اجزای مهمات خوشه‌ای (مثلاً ۱۰۰ تا ۲۰۰ قطعه) پراکنده می‌شوند؛ اندازه هر قطعه در حد چند سانتی‌متر است؛

۲) به هر قطعه یک چتر کوچک متصل است که سرعت سقوط آن را کاهش می‌دهد و در عین حال وضعیت عمودی آن را تضمین می‌کند؛

۳) یک انفجار کوچک داخلی در هر قطعه باعث شکستن آن و رهاسازی یک حلقه (قرقره) از رشته‌های کربنی می‌شود؛

۴) رشته‌های کربنی بر اثر حرکت قرقره رها شده و شبکه‌هایی همپوشان شبیه تار عنکبوت تشکیل می‌دهند؛

۵) این شبکه‌های رشته کربنی بسیار رسانا هستند و روی خطوط برق قرار می‌گیرند و نتیجه آن ایجاد جهش‌های ولتاژ است که مدارهای الکتریکی را بیش‌ازحد بارگذاری می‌کنند و در نتیجه به قطع تأمین برق می‌انجامند.

به‌طور کلی، به‌دلیل محرمانگی شدید اسناد مربوط به فناوری طراحی و توسعه بمب‌های گرافیتی، دسترسی به اطلاعات مرتبط در این زمینه دشوارتر است. با این حال، چون چنین سامانه‌هایی با بیشترین کارایی در درگیری‌های مسلحانه اخیر (یوگسلاوی سابق یا عراق) به کار رفته‌اند و علاقه عمومی به این حوزه همچنان بالاست، در ادبیات تعداد قابل‌توجهی منبع مفید درباره این سامانه تسلیحاتی به‌طور خلاصه ذکر شده است. بنابراین می‌توان نکات و جزئیات فناورانه مهمی درباره بمب‌های گرافیتی بیان کرد. ارتش آمریکا سامانه تسلیحاتی بمب بلک‌اوت CBU-94 را در خدمت دارد که از مهمات خوشه‌ای ویژه BLU-114/B برای حمله به زیرساخت تأمین برق دشمن بالقوه تشکیل شده است. اگرچه جزئیات فنی اندکی از این سامانه طبقه‌بندی‌شده شناخته شده است، سازوکار عملکرد آن را می‌توان در پراکندن مهماتی خلاصه کرد که حاوی مقدار قابل‌توجهی رشته کربنی عمل‌آوری‌شده شیمیایی است و اثر آن بر سامانه تأمین برق می‌تواند به اتصال کوتاه در برخی اجزای حساس تجهیزات (مانند ترانسفورماتورها یا پست‌های سوئیچینگ) بینجامد. استفاده از مهمات BLU-114/B محدود به عمل علیه تأسیسات تأمین برق با حداقل خطر خسارات جانبی است (از این رو نام بمب نرم).

با انفجار این مهمات روی اهداف انتخاب‌شده، تعداد زیادی رشته ظریف کربنی در هوا پخش می‌شود که ضخامت هر یک در حدود چند صدم سانتی‌متر است. این رشته‌ها می‌توانند در جو شناور بمانند و ابرهای متراکمی با ماندگاری قابل‌توجه تشکیل دهند. سپس رشته‌های فیبر کربنی پراکنده‌شده توسط مهمات BLU-114/B با ترانسفورماتورهای قدرت و سایر تجهیزات فشار قوی تماس مستقیم پیدا می‌کنند. این امر می‌تواند اتصال کوتاه ایجاد کند و غالباً جریان قوسی از میان فیبر عبور می‌کند و در نهایت فیبر تبخیر می‌شود. گرافیت که رسانای عالی برق است، احتمالاً در این مورد با مواد دیگری پوشانده شده که این اثر را تقویت می‌کنند. در ناحیه‌ای که میدان الکتریکی قوی‌ترین است، این می‌تواند تخلیه‌ای را آغاز کند و الکترون‌ها به‌سرعت کانالی یونیزه تشکیل دهند که برق را هدایت می‌کند. این امر باعث ذوب موضعی و آنی مقداری از ماده در سطح دو رسانا می‌شود. اگر جریان شدت کافی داشته باشد، این قوس می‌تواند خرابی‌های عمده یا حتی آتش‌سوزی ایجاد کند. این آتش‌سوزی می‌تواند در تجهیزات یا رساناهای بیش‌ازحد گرم‌شده بر اثر جریان بیش‌ازحد نیز آغاز شود. افزون بر این، قوس‌های الکتریکی با انرژی بسیار بالا می‌توانند با عمل خود حتی انفجار مکانیکی تجهیزات الکتریکی را موجب شوند.

اگرچه مهم‌ترین بخش جزئیات فنی طبقه‌بندی‌شده است و پنتاگون از ارائه هر گونه اطلاعاتی درباره این مهمات خودداری کرده است، بهای تمام‌شده آن احتمالاً در حدود صدها هزار دلار است. معمولاً خطای دایره‌ای این سامانه‌های هدایت‌نشونده در حد ده‌ها متر است. در آینده، با گنجاندن کیت‌های هدایت پیشرفته با دقت بالا مانند JDAM (مهمات حمله مستقیم مشترک) یا JSOW در معماری نسل بعدی بمب‌های گرافیتی، دقت و اثربخشی تخریبی این سامانه‌های تسلیحاتی بسیار افزایش خواهد یافت [۸].

شکل ۶: نمونه تصاویر سامانه تسلیحاتی CBU-97 از درگیری یوگسلاوی سابق (منبع: global security، [۷])

**نتیجه‌گیری**

نخستین نکته مهمی که از تحلیل این درگیری‌های نظامی به دست می‌آید، نسبت بسیار مطلوب بین هزینه تأسیسات تأمین برق تخریب‌شده و هزینه واقعی بمب‌های گرافیتی است. در نتیجه استفاده از چنین سلاح‌های غیرمتعارفی بسیار سودآور می‌شود. همچنین می‌توان به خسارات عظیم، تلفات انسانی عملاً حداقلی و اثر روحیه‌براندازِ ویرانگر بر ملت‌های مورد حمله و غیره اشاره کرد.

نکته مهم دیگر این است که نسل‌های متعددی از بمب‌های گرافیتی توسط ارتش آمریکا توسعه یافته است. بدین ترتیب، از مهمات مبتنی بر کیت‌های تاماهاوک که در روزهای نخست عملیات طوفان صحرا (۱۹۹۱) به کار رفت، تا مهمات BLU-114/B که به‌طور گسترده در درگیری یوگسلاوی سابق (۱۹۹۹) و عراق (۲۰۰۳) استفاده شد، و تا نسل بعدی سلاح‌های گرافیتی مبتنی بر بهره‌گیری از حامل‌های با دقت بالا مانند AGM-154 D JSOW، می‌توان نتیجه گرفت که علاقه به توسعه این نوع سامانه‌های حمله الکترونیکی غیرمتعارف همچنان بسیار بالاست (مثلاً به‌دلیل هزینه نسبتاً پایین در مقایسه با کارایی استفاده از آن و نیز تعلق به دسته بمب‌های نرم). در نهایت، همه این مزایای مهم بمب‌های گرافیتی، منابع انسانی و مالی افزونی را که در دوره آینده به آن اختصاص خواهد یافت توجیه می‌کند.

meta.pupa_reference: بمب گرافیتیت (همچنین به عنوان بمب نرم شناخته می‌شود) یک اسلحه غیر کشنده است که برای قطع سیستم تامین برق دشمن استفاده می‌شود. مکانیزم کار بمب گرافیتیت نسبتاً ساده است و بر اساس تشکیل ابرهایی از فیلامان کربنی بسیار ریز و دارویی بر روی اجزای الکتریکی بر پایه ساخت شده است. این ابرها باعث شورت‌ها و تخلیه‌های الکتریکی در زیرساخت تامین برق می‌شوند (به ویژه در نیروگاه‌ها، ایستگاه‌های ترانسفورماتور، امکانات حمل و نقل هوایی برق و غیره). علاوه بر این، استفاده موثر از این سیستم حمله الکترونیکی غیرمعمول بر اساس شناسایی نقاط حساس و فلسفه اختلال است. فیلامان‌های کربنی استفاده شده در داخل بمب‌های گرافیتیت بسیار کوچک هستند و ممکن است منجر به تشکیل ابرهای غلیظ با ماندگاری طولانی شود. همچنین، نام بمب نرم به آن‌ دلیل است که اثر مخرب اصلی آن تنها محدود به تسهیلات تامین برق است، با خطر حداقل وقوع خسارت مجاورتی و به خصوص از بین رفتن کارکنان. علاوه بر این، تأثیر بمب گرافیتیت فقط روی تجهیزات و تسهیلات برق بی‌همدرد است. شکل 1 اثرات بمب‌های گرافیتیت پرتاب شده توسط نیروی هوایی ایالات متحده در تاریخ 22 مارس 2003 بر روی یک ایستگاه ترانسفورماتور 400 کیلوولت در قدرت الکتریکی در ناصریه که باعث کاهش تامین برق در شهر برای 30 روز شد. بمب گرافیتیت در جنگ خلیج فارس اول (1990-1991) علیه عراق استفاده شد و تقریباً 85٪ از تأمین تجهیزات برق این کشور را غیرفعال کرد. همچنین، بمب گرافیتیت (تشکیل شده از زیرمجموعه‌های بی‌ال‌یو-۱۱۴ / بی) یک اجزاء تولید شده توسط ایالات متحده) در مداخله نظامی ناتو در صربستان سابق (1999) به طور گسترده استفاده شد، که اثر آن در غیرفعال سازی بیش از 70٪ تأمین برق شبکه ملی بود. اگرچه در ابتدا در کم‌تر از 24 ساعت، صرب‌ها توانستند سیستم‌های الکتریکی خود را از سر بگیرند، اما استفاده مکرر از بمب گرافیتیت به وسیله یاتآ باعث موانعی شد که همه تلاش‌های بیشتر در این جهت را به شکست بکشد. در فاز نهایی این مداخله، نیروهای هوایی ناتو اغلب از وکتورهای حامل استاندارد (مانند بمب‌ها، موشک‌ها و غیره) برای حمل و منفجر کردن مقررات در منطقه‌ای که بمب گرافیتیت عمل می‌کند، استفاده کردند. به علاو

query: You are working as a financial advisor for Mr. Buzzi, who is a well-known investor. Today Mr. Buzzi has explained to you a new business project that he has, and he wants you to prepare projected financial statements to have an idea of the profitability of the project. Following we have the data that Mr. Buzzi has delivered to you: Sales: The expected sales are 500000 units for the first year, and the sales growth is expected to be 100% for the year 2, 100% for the year 3, 120% for the year 4 and 130% for the year 5. The sales price per unit is 9€ per unit for the first year, and the estimation is that the price would be growing at a 7% every year. Variable production cost: The recipe of the product explains that the cost will be of 6€ per unit on the first and second year, and will be growing at a 2% year after year afterwards. Production labor: The first year the plant needs 6 technicians with a cost of 45000€ per person per year, 56 production workers with an annual cost of 30.000€ per employee per year, and 1 manager with a cost of 92.000€ per person per year. The next years the production labor will increase, due to the fact that the production of the plant will also be increasing. The year 2 the cost will be 50% higher than year 1, the year 3 the cost will be 50% higher than year 2, the year 4 the cost will be 55% higher than year 3 and in year 5 the cost will be 55% higher than year 4. Investment: the required investment is 13.500.000€, of which 10.000.000 will be depreciated over a period of 10 years and the rest will be depreciated over a period of 4 years. No more investments will be required during the years 2 until 5. Utilities expense: We expect a cost of 0.20€ per unit on the first year, the expectation for the following years is to have a cost increase of 4% year after year. Maintenance: the maintenance will be outsourced, and we expect a cost of 0.3 per unit produced year after year. General and administration costs are expected to be 200.000€ for the first year, 210000 for the second year, and for the following years the cost should increase in line with the sales volume, having a cost increase of 0.5% of sales of the additional sales. The days to collect accounts receivable are 90, the days to pay suppliers are 30. The company will need an inventory of 45 days. Mr. Buzzi is ready to invest 8.000.000€. The investments need to be paid upfront and the rest of money needed will come from a bank credit line, you should make your own estimation of the amount needed. The tax rate is 25% and the interest rate is 5%. Mr. Buzzi is requesting from you a proposal of Profit & loss account for the next 5 years and a balance sheet for the same period. A few weeks later, Mr Buzzi asks you to prepare a cash planning for the first year based on the following assumptions. Consider that the raw materials will be purchased on the previous month (starting in December) The raw materials inventory should be based on 45 days of the next month sales. Labor cost (also G&A) is paid divided between 12 months, always at the end of the month. Utilities and maintenance are paid every month depending on the consumption. Income tax is paid on the month of march. Interest expense is paid on the following month.

def wait_until(t):
    if not t:
        return
    h, m, s = map(int, t.split(":"))
    while True:
        now = datetime.now()
        target = now.replace(hour=h, minute=m, second=s, microsecond=0)

reference: or was our attempt in vain? Let me take you through this harrowing journey. It all began with a 3-year-old girl, Rebecca, who was brought to our emergency department. She was pale, with a rapid heartbeat, struggling to breathe, and in a state of extreme lethargy. Upon examining her, we discovered petechial rashes all over her body and a high fever. It was evident that she was critically ill, and time was of the essence. Upon further investigation, we learned that Rebecca had recently recovered from a bout of pneumonia. However, her condition rapidly deteriorated, and she was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU) for immediate attention. Blood tests revealed an alarming rise in her white blood cell count and markers of inflammation, indicating the presence of a severe infection. Given her symptoms and the rapid progression of her illness, we suspected septic shock – a life-threatening condition caused by the body's response to an infection. In septic shock, the body's immune system goes into overdrive, releasing chemicals that trigger widespread inflammation and organ dysfunction. We immediately initiated aggressive treatment, beginning with the administration of intravenous antibiotics to combat the underlying infection. Additionally, we started fluid resuscitation to stabilize her blood pressure and improve organ perfusion. However, despite our best efforts, Rebecca's condition worsened. At this critical juncture, we decided to explore alternative treatments. One option was the use of vasopressors – medications that constrict blood vessels to increase blood pressure. This approach aimed to improve blood flow to vital organs, but the risk of potential complications loomed large. With time running out, we braced ourselves for the possible consequences and initiated vasopressor therapy. Miraculously, Rebecca's blood pressure stabilized, and her organ perfusion improved. However, we were acutely aware that this was only a temporary solution. To address the root cause of her septic shock, we needed to identify the infecting organism. By conducting comprehensive laboratory tests, we were able to isolate the culprit – a strain of bacteria resistant to multiple antibiotics. Armed with this knowledge, we adjusted the antibiotic regimen accordingly, targeting the specific pathogen responsible for Rebecca's condition. Over the next few days, Rebecca's condition gradually improved. Her fever subsided, vital signs stabilized, and she regained consciousness. With each passing day, a glimmer of hope emerged amidst the chaos of the fight against septic shock. Rebecca was finally winning the race against death. Today, as I stand before you, I can proudly say that Rebecca triumphed over septic shock. It was a testament to our teamwork, quick decision-making, and relentless pursuit of a solution. The journey was not without challenges, but Rebecca's resilience, along with our unwavering commitment, led to a victory against one of the most formidable foes in pediatric medicine. In conclusion, Rebecca's case of severe septic shock serves as a reminder that every patient deserves our undivided attention, tireless effort, and innovative thinking. With continued research, improved diagnostics, and advancements in treatment modalities, we hope to see more triumphs in the face of life-threatening conditions like septic shock. Thank you for your attention, and may we always strive to emerge victorious in our race against death.

query: how can child care wokers provide support in hong kong through collaboration with parents, governments and NGOs, with apa format and references
reference:
# Supporting Children and Families in Hong Kong: Child Care Workers' Collaboration With Parents, Government, and NGOs

## Introduction

Child care workers in Hong Kong operate within a system shaped by high-pressure work cultures, dual-income families, and a mixed welfare economy in which government and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) share service delivery. Bronfenbrenner's (1979) ecological systems theory explains why collaboration matters. A child's development is influenced not only by the immediate setting (the microsystem) but also by the links between settings, such as home and center (the mesosystem), and by wider policy and community structures. Child care workers are well placed to connect these layers. This paper outlines practical ways they can do so with parents, government bodies, and NGOs.

## Collaboration With Parents

Strong family–center partnerships are associated with better developmental outcomes (Sylva et al., 2004). Epstein's (2011) framework identifies six types of involvement: parenting, communicating, volunteering, learning at home, decision-making, and collaborating with the community. Child care workers in Hong Kong can apply it as follows:

- **Two-way communication.** Use regular conferences, communication books, and messaging apps (e.g., WhatsApp), and provide information in Cantonese, English, and, where needed, other languages such as Nepali, Urdu, or Tagalog for ethnic minority and migrant families. Communication should share strengths, not only concerns (Hornby, 2011).
- **Parent education.** Hold workshops on positive discipline, screen time, school readiness, and emotional development. Working parents often need evening or weekend sessions.
- **Strengths-based, culturally responsive practice.** Recognize diverse family structures, including grandparent carers, foreign domestic helpers, and cross-boundary families, and involve all caregivers.
- **Shared decision-making.** Invite parents to join advisory groups or give feedback on curriculum and routines, consistent with dual capacity-building approaches in which both staff and families develop the skills and confidence to partner (Mapp & Kuttner, 2013).
- **Early identification and referral.** Share observations about developmental, behavioral, or welfare concerns sensitively and guide parents to appropriate services.

## Collaboration With Government

The Hong Kong government supports children and families through several departments:

- **Social Welfare Department (SWD).** Regulates child care centres and funds services such as the Child Care Centre Subsidy, extended hours services, the Neighbourhood Support Child Care Project, and Integrated Family Service Centres (Social Welfare Department, n.d.).
- **Education Bureau (EB).** Sets quality expectations for early childhood education through the Kindergarten Education Curriculum Guide (Curriculum Development Council, 2017).
- **Department of Health.** Provides Maternal and Child Health Centres and Child Assessment Services, which are important for developmental screening.
- **Commission on Children.** Established in 2018 to coordinate policies affecting children.

Child care workers can collaborate with government by:

1. **Complying with and contributing to quality standards**, including registration requirements, staff-to-child ratios, health and safety codes, and ongoing professional development.
2. **Following child protection procedures.** Workers should know and apply the multi-disciplinary guidelines for identifying and reporting suspected abuse or neglect (Social Welfare Department, 2020).
3. **Facilitating referrals** to Integrated Family Service Centres, Child Assessment Services, and the Integrated Programme in Child Care Centres for children with additional needs.
4. **Providing practice-based feedback** through consultations, professional associations, and unions so that policy reflects frontline realities.
5. **Upholding children's rights** as set out in the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (United Nations, 1989), which applies in Hong Kong.

## Collaboration With NGOs

NGOs deliver much of Hong Kong's social welfare provision and often fill service gaps. Examples include the Hong Kong Council of Social Service (HKCSS), Against Child Abuse, Save the Children Hong Kong, the Hong Kong Society for the Protection of Children, Caritas Hong Kong, and Playright Children's Play Association. Child care workers can:

- **Refer families** to counseling, parenting programs, respite care, financial assistance, and services for ethnic minority families.
- **Co-deliver programs**, such as parent–child activities, play-based learning, and community events.
- **Access training** on trauma-informed care, inclusive education, and child protection.
- **Participate in multi-agency case conferences** to coordinate support for high-risk families.
- **Join advocacy efforts** on issues such as affordable child care, workforce conditions, and children's participation.

## Strategies for Effective Multi-Party Collaboration

1. **Build shared goals and clear roles** so that parents, workers, agencies, and officials know who is responsible for what.
2. **Maintain confidentiality and ethical practice**, sharing information only as needed and in line with privacy law and professional codes.
3. **Create local networks**, such as district-level interagency meetings, to reduce fragmentation.
4. **Invest in professional development** in communication, cultural competence, and family engagement.
5. **Use evaluation and feedback loops** to review whether collaborations improve outcomes for children and families.

## Challenges and Considerations

Workers may face long hours, heavy workloads, and limited time for family engagement. Language and cultural barriers, parental stress, stigma around seeking help, and complex service pathways can also limit collaboration. Addressing these requires organizational support, adequate staffing, and policy attention to the child care workforce.

## Conclusion

By working with parents as partners, aligning with government regulation and services, and linking families to NGO resources, child care workers can create a coordinated support system around each child. Ecological and family–school partnership frameworks suggest that these connections, not isolated efforts, are what most strengthen children's wellbeing and development in Hong Kong.

## References

Bronfenbrenner, U. (1979). *The ecology of human development: Experiments by nature and design*. Harvard University Press.

Curriculum Development Council. (2017). *Kindergarten education curriculum guide*. Education Bureau, The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Epstein, J. L. (2011). *School, family, and community partnerships: Preparing educators and improving schools* (2nd ed.). Westview Press.

Hornby, G. (2011). *Parental involvement in childhood education: Building effective school-family partnerships*. Springer.

Mapp, K. L., & Kuttner, P. J. (2013). *Partners in education: A dual capacity-building framework for family–school partnerships*. SEDL and U.S. Department of Education.

Social Welfare Department. (n.d.). *Child care services*. The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region. https://www.swd.gov.hk

Social Welfare Department. (2020). *Procedural guide for handling child abuse cases* (Rev. ed.). The Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Sylva, K., Melhuish, E., Sammons, P., Siraj-Blatchford, I., & Taggart, B. (2004). *The Effective Provision of Pre-School Education (EPPE) project: Final report*. Department for Education and Skills / Institute of Education, University of London.

United Nations. (1989). *Convention on the rights of the child*. https://www.ohchr.org/en/instruments-mechanisms/instruments/convention-rights-child

---

*Note:* Hong Kong policies, program names, and guidelines are updated often. Check the SWD and EB websites for current versions and add retrieval dates for web sources if your instructor requires them. Confirm each reference against your library database before submitting.

For example, “I will document all my work and share my progress in weekly team meetings.” Measurable: Objectives need to be quantifiable. Measurable objectives give concrete information. For example, “I will produce three interim reports and one final report.” Including quantitative information makes it possible to determine whether the objective has been met. Achievable: Objectives need to be reasonable and achievable. Initially, many students believe they can achieve more than what is reasonable given the available time, resources and so on. She never made any major moves to solidify whether or not she was in to me or just saw me as a really good friend. I spent all summer thinking about her, missing all the time that I had grown used to spending with her. I watched summer tik away slowly as I impatiently waited for school to start back up again. Our relationship was starting to feel like it was in a better place than when summer started. Near the end of October she told me that there was going to be this killer costume party and she wanted me to go with her. She was going as a witch and asked if I would be her peasant slave. I thought it was a weird request, but at the same time, this was sounding very much like a couples costume. At this point I had already developed very strong feeling for her and would do whatever it took for an opportunity to win her over, so I happily agreed. The night of the party she came to pick me up. The party was a decent ways off campus, tucked away in the middle of nowhere, so as to avoid cops coming to shut down the party. I was pretty excited. She made for one hot witch, and I didn't care if my costume was kind of demeaning because it made her so happy that we could go together. When we got there I noticed that there weren't a lot of familiar faces, but the party was bumpin either way so I didn't care nor think much of it. As the night carried on she drug me around with her everywhere, showing off our costumes, often joking about how she planned on taking me back to her lair for her dinner. She kept handing me beer after beer, I assumed trying to get me to loosen up. I'm not the most social person ever and can get kind of shy in groups. Her plan was working however. The more I drank the easier it was to open up and enjoy myself. It had started getting late and a lot of people had already made their way home. There were still a few stragglers, ourselves included. She took me by the hand and led me into a big empty room. She turned to look at me and grabbed me by the hand. "You've been a good little peasant slave," she said with a giggle and a wink. "Now, being the generous witch that I am, I'll grant you one free wish! What'll it be!?" I was heavily intoxicated, and as I looked at her gorgeous face, only one thing came to mind. "I just want to be yours forever." As soon as I said it I froze up. I hadn't thought before I spoke, and now it was all out there. I guess now I would finally get my definitive answer. A smile formed on her black lips. "What would you do to prove that you're worthy to be mine?" Was she serious? Did I actually stand a chance!? "I would do anything your heart desires," I said as sweetly as my drunken self could muster. She reached into her purse and pulled out salt and a candle. I was confused but just watched as she made a ring of salt on the floor and lit the candle in the middle of it. "I will give you the ultimate test then," she said stepping out of the circle after lighting the candle. "Step inside the circle." I did as she said and she started to mumble words I couldn't understand.

Rose and I are going to have so much fun today!” he exclaimed, his excitement contagious. Joseph chuckled at his son's enthusiasm and playfully asked, “So, now you want me out of your way huh?” he nodded. I couldn't help but smile at their banter. It was heartwarming to see the bond between father and son and to feel Joseph's genuine concern for me. query: Ledbury Poetry (UK) has announced that Donegal poet Annemarie Ní Churreáin is among the poets shortlisted for the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize for best second collection published in Britain or Ireland in 2021 or 2022. The prize aims to support and encourage poets at the mid-career stage, with a prize of £5000 for the winning second collection. Speaking of Ní Churreáin’s nominated work, judges Togara Muzanenhamo and Penelope Shuttle said: “Drawing inspiration from the concept of restorative justice – Annemarie Ní Churreáin’s The Poison Glen entwines legend from the Gaeltacht landscape with moments from history to depict the systematic mistreatment of unmarried or abandoned mothers and the children born to these women. Ní Churreáin revisits locations of state care institutions in Ireland over the past hundred years and beyond with an inquisitive lens that requires us to ask what the left-behind sites remember or what sense of the child remains after trauma. The Poison Glen stands as a literary monument to silenced voices”. ADVERTISEMENT - CONTINUE READING BELOW Originally from Cloich Cheann Fhaola, Ní Churreáin's books include Bloodroot, Doire Press, 2017, Town, The Salvage Press, 2018, and The Poison Glen, The Gallery Press, 2021. She is a recipient of the Irish Arts Council’s Next Generation Artist Award and a co-recipient of The Markievicz Award. She is Poetry Editor at The Stinging Fly Magazine. Her most recent literary project, a limited edition poetry pamphlet titled Ghostgirl, explores the Stranorlar Workhouse and Stranorlar County Home, also known as Stranorlar Mother and Baby Home. The project was a commission of the Donegal Archives Service as part of the Donegal Decade of Centenaries Programme. Co-judge Togara Muzanenhamo said: “The award is particularly special because it celebrates the accomplishment of what can be an artistic hurdle for some poets – compiling a second collection. There are numerous prizes for first collections and best collections but few focus on the pivotal role of a poets’ second book – a book that may highlight a poet’s maturing voice or solidify their career. I am excited at the prospect of reading work that will confidently explore and freely navigate language and introduce us to voices that will shape the future of poetry”. The winner of the fourth Ledbury Hellens Poetry Prize will be announced on December 4 at 7pm at an online prize giving ceremony hosted by the Ledbury Centre.

- 2.0/8.4 = 0.238095

Using the given n instead:

- 0.000086 × 62.36 = 0.00536296
- × 329 = 1.764462

reference: To calculate the standard error of a sample proportion, we can use the formula: Standard error = sqrt((p̂ * (1 - p̂)) / n) Where: - p̂ is the sample proportion - n is the sample size In this case, the sample proportion is 73% or 0.73, and the sample size is 100. Standard error = sqrt((0.73 * (1 - 0.73)) / 100) Calculating this expression: Standard error = sqrt((0.5329) / 100) = sqrt(0.005329) ≈ 0.073 Therefore, the standard error of the sample proportion is approximately 0.073, which is equivalent to 0.063 when rounded to two decimal places.
