query: first separate input: 'CHAPTER 1 INTRODUCTION In this chapter, we describe the research background with respect to hand kinematics analysis methods and state-of-art studies of hand and fingers tracking system, then we show the significance of researches for hand and fingers tracking technology in various fields (section 1.1). Next we state our research motivation (section 1.2), and we present overall contribution and innovations of the research (section 1.3). We finish up with the basic organization of the following of the thesis (section 1.4). 1.1 Research Background and Significance Recent researches have focused on developing hand and high-precision finger motion detection systems for a variety of applications based on tracking methods, such as robotics, virtual reality, and medicine Rehabilitation. Some of those applications are as follow: -Robotics: The most popular study field in robotics is the manufacture of prostherix hands. Researchers design prototype of an underactuated prosthetic hand, which improve the range of motion and dexterity of thumb and pinch and innovatively restore the capability of the thumb-index pinch [1]. -Virtual reality: Hand movement is the main means of interacting with the environment, so it is crucial in virtual reality (VR) applications. Although the existing inverse kinematics motion detection is sufficient for full body tracking (Fig.1.1) [2], it is difficult to locate small body parts such as fingers, and these parts are often blocked in the optical detection process. VR professionals need additional systems (such as inertial trackers) with low reliability [3]. -Medicine Rehabilitation: A 5-DOF hand rehabilitation robot is designed and developed using a synthetic method for generating natural curved finger tip motion using a 1-DOF mechanism (Fig.1.2). It’s practical in the diagnosis and treatment of hand injuries and diseases [4]. With the help of advanced sensors and computer vision methods, those system is able to capture and analyze finger movements. Machine learning algorithms are often used to interpret the data and provide real-time feedback to users [5,6] . These studies give us examples and inspires of the importance of hand-finger motion detection in different industries, and also show promise in improving the accuracy of the finger motion detection and tracking system. However, there are still challenges in developing a compact and comfortable system for users to wear and use for a long time, as well as its applicability in more application scenarios. 1.2 Motivation The existing research has done enough detail in measuring and tracking hand movements, and has derived many extensions and applications in various fields. However, the bending and extension of a single finger is different from the movement of the entire hand, and the detection of finger movement becomes very difficult when moving or rotating. In current finger motion detection technology, there are two distinct categories can be distinguished depending on the use of cameras or individual sensors. -Vision based: Use passive optical motion capture technology by setting cameras to capture the dynamic image of a specially designed glove with markers, then use the machine vision technique to process the images and correlate the local variation of image to the motion of fingers or change in the hand gesture [7,8]. The vision based hand tracking system has non-contact perception function, making hand motion detection convenient and efficient. Besides, machine vision and imaging analysis based on camara involve expensive components and complex algorithms [9], which are very expensive for ordinary users. The main advantage of a vision based system is its high tracking accuracy, but it has drawbacks such as sensitivity to light intensity fluctuations and occlusion issues, which may lead to tracking errors [10]. -Sensors based: The sensor-based systems directly detect the motion and bending of the fingers using various types of sensors such as accelerometers [4], gyroscopes, magnetic sensors, resistive sensors, and ElectroMyoGraphy (EMG) sensors [11] etc. To a certain it can help to mitigate the problem of vision-based system. Besides, the sensor-based systems are also in general more compact and inexpensive. However, acceleration or inertial sensors are generally susceptible to gravitational artifacts due to the rotation and vibration of arms or bodies. In our research, we intend to design and develop a magnetic sensors based device which is hihgly compact and have ability to detect finger motions real-time accurately. Because magnetic sensors have advantages over limitations of vision based systems which severely restricted the adoption of hand tracking in real-world applications (bulky tethered systems is impractical and line of sight or privacy concerns) [12]. Finger tips are significant marks of hand kinematics analysis, which have fewer amounts than joint angles of fingers and simpler structure. We intend to fix a magnetic sensor on each fingertips and a permanent magnet on the dorsal side of the hand to detect finger motions. Since the magnetic permeability of the human body is very similar to air, water and other non-ferromagnetic materials, it does not affect the static magnetic field [13]. The low-cost, compact, and accessible hand-finger motion tracking system is possible. 1.3 Contributions We propose a magnetic hand-finger motion tracking system which is simple, compact, low-cost, accurate and unobstructive for intelligent human-computer interface and various other applications involving hand gestures recognization. The core principle is relative fingertips position estimating with the use of magnetic sensors, then detect the hand gestures from the orientation and locations of the fingertips. The main contributions of our research are: 1. A intelligent finger motion tracking system using magnetic sensors is porposed. For sensors detecting part of the system, we choose the scheme that measure the orientations and locations of sensors in motion in a stationary magnetic field created by one permanent magnet. A permanent magnet is fixed on the dorsal side of the hand. Five 9-axis IMUs is settled on each of the fingertips, and one 6-axis IMU is fixed with the permanent magnet in order to achieve the attitude calibration and distance measurement between IMUs. After we get the result of finger motion by combining each 9-axis sensors’ orientations and locations (angular velocity on 3-axis, acceleration rate on 3-axis, and magnetic flux density on 3-axis), the next step is to adopt deep learning approaches to realize the real-time gesture recognization function. Various common gestures can be displayed as corresponding patterns when we make actual movements. 2. A set of algorithms for computing orientations and locations of sensors on the fingertips are proposed. First, we use EKF method for estimating the orientations of the 9-axis sensors on the fingertips to the 6-axis sensors on the dorsal side of the hand. After orthogonalization the coordinate system of two sensors through matrix operation, we apply L-M algorithm to calculate the linear distance between those two sensors to get the locations of 9-axis sensors. The L-M algorithm is based on a dipole model which approximate the magnet as a dipole under the research condition. Our experiments show the dipole model satisfied high approximation and accuracy within a certain range which is sufficient for finger motion tracking and gesture recognization. 3. A DNN method is adopted to achieve the real-time gesture recognization function. DNN map the features of existing spatial samples to another feature space through layer by layer feature mapping, in order to learn better feature representation for existing inputs. Firstly we maintain the posture of a specified gesture on the device and create positional data of the gesture in three-dimensional space through the movements and rotations of the hand and wrist. Then we cyclically group and train all data to obtain high accuracy in both training and testing sets. Finally, we use the wearable device to continuously make any gesture in the gesture library, the terminal can accurately display the corresponding gesture pattern. We develop our device prototype on a SBC: Raspberry pi 4b. It is also fixed on the dorsal side of hand aiming to read data and computing the orientations and locations of sensors. The data from 9-axis sensors are transmitted by I2C bus real-timely to the SBC for the next step of attitude calibration and distance calculation. Besides, we use our originally designed PCB to achieve improvements on stability and integration. Finally we fabricate prototype device on a left-hand glove, improve the compactness and comfort additionally. '

query: расскажи про PR-кампанию Coca-Cola “Share a Coke"
reference: Кампания "Share a Coke" была запущена Coca-Cola в 2011 году в Австралии и Новой Зеландии и быстро стала мировым хитом. Это была первая кампания, в рамках которой были заменены стандартные надписи на банках и бутылках Coca-Cola именами потребителей. Главная идея PR-кампании заключалась в том, чтобы способствовать более тесному общению между людьми. Coca-Cola считает, что этот напиток — не просто банальный продукт питания, он может объединять людей, поэтому в качестве etiltes предлагалась наладить общение с разными людьми, поделиться напитком и порадовать близких. Компания проводила рекламную кампанию в социальных сетях, печатных изданиях, телевидении, на сайте и в магазинах. Многие стали постить фотографии с банками Coca-Cola в социальных сетях с хэштегом #shareacoke, что способствовало еще большей популяризации кампании. Стоит отметить, что эта кампания оказалась беспрецедентно успешной и, по словам сотрудников Coca-Cola, превзошла все ожидания. Она получила международное признание и была запущена во многих странах мира. Бренд также продолжил кампанию вплоть до недавнего времени, добавив новые имена на банки и бутылки Coca-Cola и предложив потребителям напечатать свои имена и создать персонализированную банку.

This is a non-personal services contract. Contractor employees are not subject to supervision or control by Government personnel.

query: Coastal restoration and rehabilitation offer great promise for vulnerable and marginalized groups in need of adaptation. However in Kenya, a critical research gap in evidence-based policy discussions demands immediate attention to advance these efforts towards building resilience for the most vulnerable segments of society. Presently, there is a lack of a dedicated community-led framework and relevant indicators that can effectively align coastal restoration and rehabilitation initiatives with the priorities of different social groups, especially those who are vulnerable and marginalized, such as women, children, indigenous communities, persons with disabilities, and minorities, all residing within the coastal regions. Additionally, there is a pressing need to establish methods for measuring and reporting the effectiveness of these restoration and rehabilitation efforts in addressing the intersectional vulnerabilities within these communities. Furthermore, linking the lessons learned from these initiatives to national adaptation plans and NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions) is essential for ensuring a comprehensive approach to coastal resilience and safeguarding the interests of the vulnerable populations. The project aims to co-create locally led restoration indicators with the established community of practices and all the stakeholders through development of evidence based policy labs. Our project main goals: 1. To map out all stakeholders and establish a community of practice in coastal conservation and restoration. 2. To assess Policy, Institutional Framework and Knowledge gaps on coastal ecosystem restoration initiatives. 3. To assess the locally led restoration activities undertaken by different community groups. 4. To work with different local community groups to co-develop and agree on indicators that capture priority restoration actions and their expectations of impacts based on the assessed gaps 5. Co-development of impact learning and conservation framework: Based on the assessments, we will develop learning materials on restoration and conservation of coastal ecosystems and a conservation framework that targets the specific needs of coastal communities. 6. Establishment of multi stakeholder policy labs that will target all stakeholders and community of practice implementing restoration programs. These will be trained on Locally led restoration metrics co-production and development

query: summarise into bullet points: When I am emailed by pupils studying The Woman in Black for GCSE and A-level, many refer to it as "gothic", and indeed it forms part of a university course in gothic literature. But although the book has something in common with the pure gothic fiction of the 18th and 19th centuries, it is really only a distant cousin of the genre. It is a ghost story – not a horror story, not a thriller – and not a gothic novel; although the terms are often used very loosely, they are not by any means the same thing. I set out to write a ghost story in the classic 19th-century tradition, a full-length one. There have never been many, writers perhaps having felt the form would not stretch successfully. By the time I began mine, in the 1980s, full-length ghost stories seemed to have died out altogether. I read and studied the Jameses, Henry and MR, and Dickens, and I also had beside me the "bible" – Night Visitors by Julia Briggs (still the best study of the form). The list of ingredients included atmosphere, a ghost, a haunted house and other places, and weather. A footnote to "ghost" was a) of a human being; and b) with a purpose. There are dozens of little books of "true" ghost stories, usually sorted by geographical location, but almost without exception the ghosts have no purpose and so the stories are ultimately unsatisfying. A headless horseman rides by, a phantom coach clatters down a dark road, a veiled lady drifts up a staircase and through a wall, a pale and misty child's face is glimpsed at a window – and that is all. The ghosts are there and they apparently go through the same motions again and again. It is ultimately uninteresting. There has to be more to fiction than that. There also has to be more than an easy manipulation of the reader's superficial emotions – unless making someone jump out of their skin is the writer's only aim. Not that trying to induce a delicious thrill of fear is bad – it is another form of entertainment, and what is wrong with being an entertainer? Dickens certainly considered himself to be one. I knew my ghost story, like all my fiction, had to have a serious point and it was this that must sustain the length and underpin the sense of place, the creation of atmosphere and the events. But moral points come out of character, and I kept asking myself the question: "Why does a ghost return to this life?" Perhaps to give information that they have withheld in life – the whereabouts of a will, say, or the identity of a murderer, or to warn. But my ghost returns to exact revenge and it is the nature of revenge that it is never satisfied; and so, loss and grief lead the woman in black on, trying to exact revenge for her child's accidental death by causing those of others. She cannot let go, and her revenge is an evil that continues to be visited on Crythin Gifford. The grief and craving for revenge must be released or she cannot find resolution and peace on either side of the grave. So here was my central character. Why a "woman in black"? I must have had Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White in mind but it was more than 25 years since I had read his novel. Otherwise, I have no clear idea where she came from. Thomas Hardy believed that places are as important as people in fiction, because people are formed by the landscapes in which they are born and bred, though that is probably less true now than it was in his day, when, especially in rural areas, they tended to remain rooted in one place. But a harsh climate and a hard landscape toughen people. A low-lying, dank place tends to be lowering to the spirits, and we all know that constant wind drives people mad. I think the pathetic fallacy is less fallacious than is often supposed. I don't know where the plot of the book came from, partly because I never do know, partly because it is too long ago. But I remember one thing. In the early 1970s I worked by the sea, behind which were the marshes. Walking there at dusk, the light making the gleam and the low wind rattle the reeds, was when I began to think seriously about ghosts. It seemed natural to adopt a rather formal style and that came along with the point of view. I had to write in the first person. The narrator, Arthur Kipps, is the living key to the book, just as the woman in black is the dead one.

# How PESTLE Factors Shape McDonald's: A Closer Look

Few brands are as instantly recognisable as the Golden Arches. But behind the familiar fries and Big Macs, McDonald's is constantly wrestling with forces far beyond its control. Here's how each PESTLE factor affects the company, with evidence.

## Political: Caught in the Crossfire

McDonald's is a global brand, so it can't escape global politics. When Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022, the company made the painful decision to leave Russia after 30 years, selling roughly 850 restaurants. It cost the company around $1.2-1.4 billion. That wasn't just a business decision; it was a moral one that meant walking away from 62,000 employees' workplaces (the company continued paying them for a period).

The Israel-Gaza conflict also hit hard. After a franchisee in Israel offered free meals to Israeli soldiers in 2023, boycotts spread across Muslim-majority countries such as Malaysia and Indonesia. McDonald's admitted in 2024 that the conflict had a "meaningful" impact on its sales, and its CEO, Chris Kempczinski, described the business impact as significant.

## Economic: Squeezed from Every Side

Rising inflation has turned the "value" promise into a sore point. Between 2019 and 2024, menu prices in the US rose by around 40%, and customers noticed. A viral backlash over $18 Big Mac meals prompted McDonald's to launch the $5 Meal Deal in 2024 to win back budget-conscious diners. In 2024, the company reported falling traffic among low-income customers, a sign of how fragile the relationship with the cash-strapped consumer can be.

## Social: Changing Tastes, Changing Values

People increasingly want healthier, more ethical food. The rise of plant-based eating led McDonald's to trial the McPlant burger (developed with Beyond Meat), though it was ultimately shelved in the US after lukewarm demand, a reminder that good intentions don't always translate into sales. Meanwhile, concerns about obesity and ultra-processed foods continue to shape public perception. On the flip side, social media has been kind: the Travis Scott meal (2020) and the Grimace Birthday Meal (2023) went viral and drove huge sales among younger customers.

## Technological: Racing to Stay Relevant

Convenience is king. Digital sales now exceed $30 billion annually across the company's top markets, driven by the mobile app, self-order kiosks and delivery partnerships with Uber Eats and DoorDash. McDonald's also tested AI-powered drive-through ordering with IBM, but ended the trial in 2024 after viral videos showed orders going comically wrong, such as hundreds of chicken nuggets being added by mistake. Innovation is exciting, but it's risky when the whole world is watching.

## Legal: Rules That Bite

McDonald's faces a maze of regulations. In the EU, it was caught up in a tax dispute with Luxembourg, though the European Commission ruled in 2018 that no illegal state aid was given. In the US, the company has faced lawsuits over alleged workplace harassment and has been scrutinised as a "joint employer" of franchise workers. In California, the 2024 law raising the fast-food minimum wage to $20 an hour pushed up labour costs and menu prices for franchisees.

## Environmental: The Pressure to Do Better

For a company serving millions daily, the footprint is enormous. Beef production is a major source of greenhouse gases, and McDonald's has pledged to reach net-zero emissions by 2050 and to source packaging from renewable, recycled or certified sources. It has phased out plastic straws in several markets and introduced paper alternatives, although critics argue progress on packaging waste is slow. Deforestation tied to the supply chain remains a reputational risk, and activists have been vocal about it.

## The Bottom Line

McDonald's survives by being adaptable, but PESTLE shows how vulnerable even a giant can be. Politics can close doors overnight, economics can anger loyal customers, and one viral clip can undo years of tech investment. The brands that thrive are those that listen and adapt before the storm hits.

*Note: Figures are approximate and drawn from public reporting up to 2024; check McDonald's annual reports for the latest data before citing in formal work.*

Verify the MongoDB connection string: Double-check the connection string for any typos or incorrect values. Ensure that the hostname, port, username, password, and other connection parameters are correct. 2. Check network connectivity: Ensure that you have a stable internet connection and can reach the MongoDB server from your local machine. Confirm that there are no network configuration issues or firewall restrictions preventing the connection. 3. DNS configuration: Ensure that your DNS settings are configured correctly and can resolve the MongoDB hostname. You can try using alternative DNS servers, such as Google DNS (8.8.8.8) or Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1). 4. Temporary network issues: The "ENOTFOUND" error can occur due to temporary network issues or outages. In such cases, retrying the connection after some time may resolve the problem. You can also check MongoDB status or contact your hosting provider to ensure there are no known issues. 5. Verify MongoDB hostname: Check that the MongoDB hostname you are using is correct and reachable. You can try connecting to the MongoDB server using tools like `ping` or `nslookup` to validate the hostname resolution. 6. Check MongoDB server status: Ensure that the MongoDB server you are trying to connect to is running and accessible. Confirm that the server is correctly configured and accepting incoming connections. reference:
# Zoom Interview Scenario: Freelance Graphic Designer

**Candidate:** Amer
**Role:** Freelance Graphic Designer (brand identity and social media project)
**Interviewer:** Sarah Collins, Marketing Manager at BrightPath Studio
**Duration:** About 30 minutes

---

## 1. Opening (2–3 min)

**Sarah:** Hi Amer, thanks for joining. Can you hear and see me okay?

**Amer:** Hi Sarah, yes, loud and clear. Thanks for having me.

**Sarah:** Great. Before we start, how's your day going?

**Amer:** Very good, thank you. I'm excited to talk about the project.

---

## 2. Introduction (3–4 min)

**Sarah:** Tell me a bit about yourself and your design background.

**Amer:** I'm Amer, a freelance graphic designer with [X] years of experience. I specialize in brand identity, logo design, and social media graphics. I've worked with startups, cafés, and e-commerce brands, helping them build a consistent visual style that stands out. I enjoy turning a client's rough idea into a clear, memorable design.

---

## 3. Portfolio Discussion (7–8 min)

**Sarah:** Could you share your screen and walk me through a project you're proud of?

**Amer:** Sure. *(shares screen)* This is a rebrand I did for a local coffee shop. They wanted to attract a younger audience while keeping their warm, traditional feel. I researched competitors, built a mood board, then created three logo concepts. The final design used a modern wordmark with a hand-drawn coffee bean icon and an earthy color palette. After the rebrand, their Instagram engagement grew by about 40% in two months.

**Sarah:** How did you handle client feedback?

**Amer:** I ask for feedback in specific terms, like "What feels off about the color?" rather than "Do you like it?" I also set a limit of two or three revision rounds at the start to keep the project on track.

---

## 4. Skills and Process Questions (7–8 min)

**Sarah:** What tools do you use?

**Amer:** Mainly Adobe Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign. I use Figma for collaboration and Canva when clients need editable templates.

**Sarah:** How do you manage tight deadlines?

**Amer:** I break the project into milestones, share a timeline upfront, and send progress updates. If something might cause a delay, I tell the client early rather than at the last minute.

**Sarah:** Tell me about a difficult client situation.

**Amer:** A client once kept changing the direction mid-project. I scheduled a short call to re-align on goals, documented everything in a creative brief, and agreed that further changes would be handled as an add-on. That kept things professional and the client was happy with the result.

---

## 5. Business Questions (3–4 min)

**Sarah:** How do you price your work and handle payment?

**Amer:** I offer project-based pricing depending on scope. I take 50% upfront and 50% on delivery. Final files are released after full payment.

**Sarah:** What's your availability?

**Amer:** I can start next week and take on about 15–20 hours weekly for this project.

---

## 6. Candidate Questions and Closing (3–4 min)

**Amer:** Could you tell me more about your brand style and target audience? And what does success look like for this project?

**Sarah:** *(answers)* Thanks, Amer. We'll review everything and get back to you by Friday.

**Amer:** Thank you, Sarah. I'll send over my portfolio link and a couple of references after this call. Have a great day!

---

## Quick Zoom Tips for Amer

- **Test** your camera, mic, and internet 10 minutes early.
- **Prepare** your portfolio in a tab, ready to share, and close unnecessary windows and notifications.
- **Lighting and background:** face a light source and keep the background tidy.
- **Look at the camera** when speaking, not just the screen.
- **Have notes ready:** 2–3 case studies with the problem, process, and result.
- **Follow up** with a thank-you email within 24 hours.

---

This crash is most likely **not caused by your Unity code**. It's a native crash inside Android's own graphics stack, on an emulator.

## What the trace says

- **Thread:** `RenderThread`. This is the Android HWUI render thread, not Unity's thread.
- **Crash path:** `eglSwapBuffers` → `Surface::queueBuffer` → `BLASTBufferQueue::onFrameAvailable` → `acquireNextBufferLocked` → `SurfaceComposerClient::Transaction::merge` → `RefBase::decStrong` → `__android_log_assert` → `abort`.
- **Meaning:** a reference-counting assertion failed in `libutils` (`RefBase::decStrong`) while BLASTBufferQueue was merging surface transactions. That is an Android framework bug (a ref-count or use-after-free race), not a managed or IL2CPP error.
- **Device:** `google/sdk_gphone64_arm64`, Android 13 (`TE1A.220922.034`, `userdebug`). This is the Android Studio emulator. The `libEGL_emulation.so` frame confirms it.
- **Unity:** 2020.3.21f1, which is old. It predates a lot of Android 12/13 compatibility fixes.

## Likely triggers

1. A bug in the emulator's system image (Android 13 early builds, `TE1A.220922`). BLASTBufferQueue had several known races.
2. Surface lifecycle problems, such as rotating the screen, pausing or resuming, resizing, or switching the window while rendering.
3. Unity 2020.3.21 handling surface destruction or recreation poorly on Android 12 and later.

## What to try

1. **Test on a real device.** If it doesn't crash there, it's an emulator problem and you can mostly ignore it.
2. **Update the emulator and system image.** In Android Studio's SDK Manager, update the Emulator and install a newer Android 13 image (a later security patch) or API 34. Also try a "Google APIs" image instead of the `userdebug` one.
3. **Change the emulator graphics setting.** In the AVD settings, switch Graphics from Automatic to *Software* or *Hardware*, whichever you aren't using now. Cold boot the AVD afterwards.
4. **Update Unity** to the latest 2020.3 LTS (2020.3.48f1 or later), or to 2021 LTS or newer. Later versions contain many Android surface and swapchain fixes.
5. **Check your Player settings:**
   - Try switching between Vulkan and OpenGLES3 under Auto Graphics API. Emulators handle Vulkan poorly, so OpenGLES3 is usually more stable.
   - Disable "Optimized Frame Pacing" if it's enabled.
   - Check the resolution and orientation settings. Try a fixed orientation to see whether the crash only happens on rotation.
6. **Find the trigger.** Note what you were doing when it crashed (app start, backgrounding, rotating, loading a scene). Then check `adb logcat` just before the abort for lines like `BLASTBufferQueue` or `Fatal signal 6`. The assertion message, such as `decStrong() called on ... too many times`, will be right before the abort.

## Bottom line

This is a platform-level crash in the emulator's Android image, triggered by the rendering and surface lifecycle. Test on a physical device first. If you only see it on the emulator, update the emulator and system image and switch the graphics mode. If it also happens on real devices, upgrade Unity and share the logcat lines just before the crash so we can narrow down the trigger.

By using game theory, Ralph can increase his chances of success and bring childhood dreams, like owning a new bike, closer to reality.

query: Structure and optimize the following focus plan: Background: Aly has been with Amazon for 12 months, He joined VF team in July of 22’’ as city manager for West Cairo shortly before PEAK and showed high ownership and bias for action and was rated as an HV2. Shortly after PEAK, and starting in Jan 23’’, Aly faced a few health-related family issues that started to clearly affect his focus, performance and output. He requested multiple personal leaves, and the team offered support to cover for him. After things seemingly started to get better on the personal aspects, his performance never picked up, rather, it continued to slack. Performance Assessment: As a City manager Aly is responsible for all West Cairo sites, 5 of which are critical- high volume VF sites with Amazon AAs on ground. Aly is tasked with all on ground operations, IB control, stock control, AA performance, TPH, labor management and their development for all of his sites. On ground Ops: Aly has not been fully present on ground for the past couple of months and has been relying more on the on-ground supervisor to control operations hence multiple issues are not being identified on time and handled properly. In addition, a few instances occurred where even when he was present on ground he failed (or chose not to) to communicate high risk impactful issues to his superiors, pears or relevant stakeholders which led to tons of extra work on the team’s end and at times translated to actual misses impacting overall team metrics and performance. IB and stock Control: Continuous gaps have been found in both areas with multiple promises of remediation on his end with no appropriate output. Issues have not been brought to leadership attention on time, because of vague, incomplete or untrue answers to follow-up questions which resulted in a significant trust breach between Aly and the team. AA performance and TPH: Due to his lack of presence on ground, TPH has been dropping from its BAU value and AA’s performance has been slacking. Multiple instances occurred where items were poorly packed, lost, shipped without AWBs, etc.. A clear lack of control, follow up and proper training has been identified and communicated to Aly without proper actions taken on his end to fix it. Initial Performance Assessment Conclusion: Aly’s continuous drop in performance and irresponsiveness to feedback, along with serious concerns on earning trust has led the team to decide on putting him on focus to communicate the gaps more assertively and track performance progress very closely. Task, goals and actions should be communicated to him in details, with clear milestones, deliverables and deadlines in order to assess his progress properly. Development Areas; 1- Work on earning back team’s trust by communicating more clearly and truthfully in a timely manner. 2- Take back control of on ground ops, by being more present and DDing into all matters in question. 3- Work on better tracking AA’s performance & TPH, identify gaps and work in depth to develop and train AAs and optimize TPH. 4- Keep track of data and volumes to better manage and communicate labor needs, and optimize rooster. 5- Work on his communication skills with the team and relevant stakeholders to be able to callout critical issues on time. 6- Work on better understanding priorities, criticalities and time sensitivity of his tasks.

On-Ground Operations Management: - Clearly define Aly's responsibilities as the city manager for all West Cairo sites, including on-ground operations, IB control, stock control, AA performance, TPH, labor management, and development. - Emphasize the importance of Aly being fully present on the ground and actively involved in operations. - Schedule regular on-site visits for Aly to monitor operations, identify issues, and provide support to the on-ground supervisor. - Implement a system for Aly to report and escalate high-risk issues promptly to superiors, peers, and relevant stakeholders. - Monitor Aly's presence and involvement in on-ground operations and provide feedback on improvements. 3. AA Performance and TPH Optimization: - Regularly review AA performance and TPH metrics with Aly. - Identify gaps in training and development for AAs and provide resources and support to address these gaps. - Set clear expectations for AA performance, proper packing, tracking, and follow-up processes. - Implement a performance tracking system to monitor improvements in TPH and AA performance. - Provide regular feedback and coaching to Aly on optimizing AA performance and TPH. 4. Labor Management and Optimization: - Work with Aly to establish a system to track data and volumes for better labor management. - Define clear goals and targets for labor optimization, including roster management. - Regularly review labor needs and align resources accordingly to avoid understaffing or overstaffing. - Provide training and support to Aly on labor management techniques and effective communication with relevant stakeholders. 5. Communication Skills Enhancement: - Offer communication skills training to Aly, focusing on effectively conveying critical issues and time sensitivity. - Provide resources and guidance on prioritization techniques to help Aly better understand and manage his tasks. - Encourage regular communication and feedback sessions to practice and improve communication skills. - Provide ongoing support and guidance to Aly in developing his communication skills with the team and relevant stakeholders. 6. Progress Tracking: - Establish regular progress check-ins with Aly to assess his progress in addressing the development areas. - Monitor and review milestones, deliverables, and deadlines to ensure progress is being made. - Provide constructive feedback and guidance on areas where improvement is still needed. - Celebrate and acknowledge achievements and improvements made by Aly. By implementing this focus plan, Aly will have clear goals and actions to work on, allowing for better performance assessment and improvement in his role as the city manager for West Cairo.

A., Blake, J., DeFrancesco, M. S., DeNicola, N., Martin Jr, J. N., ... & Giudice, L. C. (2015). reference: **Study Overview and Implications** The groundbreaking research conducted by Di Renzo et al. (2015) aimed to elucidate the reproductive health impacts of exposure to toxic environmental chemicals. The study meticulously outlined how various common environmental pollutants, such as pesticides, air pollutants, metals, and endocrine-disrupting chemicals, adversely affect the health of pregnant women, fetuses, and reproductive outcomes. One pivotal finding from this research is the discernible link between exposure to these chemicals and a range of adverse health outcomes, including preterm birth, low birth weight, and developmental defects. Expectant mothers stand as one of the primary audiences who can greatly benefit from these findings. The study not only raises awareness about the potential dangers these women face from environmental pollutants but also empowers them with knowledge, potentially guiding them in mitigating unnecessary exposures. Understanding this risk profile may encourage expectant mothers to advocate for safer environmental practices and regulations, seek out environments with better air quality, and be more vigilant about avoiding high-risk substances. Families and married couples planning for children could also utilize this information by adjusting lifestyle choices and domestic environments to foster healthier reproductive outcomes. Knowledge of toxic substances at play could transform the choices they make, influencing their residential decisions, consumer behavior, and even political engagement to support environmental reforms for safer communities. Young people exposed to stress and addictive substances are another significant group that could stand to gain knowledge from this research. Often on the cusp of their reproductive years, understanding the long-term implications of their exposure could inform better life decisions, aid in lobbying for healthier college campuses and work environments, and inspire engagement with public health initiatives that target environmental health. Healthcare professionals, as key interpreters and implementers of such research, can integrate these findings into their practice by increased screening for environmental exposures, offering advice for risk reduction, and continuing education to stay abreast of new research. They can also contribute to the broader dialogue on environmental health policy, bolstered by evidence-based understanding of these risks. **Limitations of the Study** Despite the valuable insights garnered from the study by Di Renzo et al. (2015), several limitations warrant consideration. Firstly, the global nature of this research brings variability in environmental laws, exposure levels, and health outcomes that may not apply uniformly across different populations. Hence, the transferability and applicability of the findings may require regional adaptation. Secondly, the mixed-method approaches of correlating reproductive outcomes with environmental exposures face challenges of causal inferences due to potential confounding factors. Lifestyle, genetic predispositions, and other environmental factors not wholly accounted for might skew the perceived impacts of toxic chemicals. Furthermore, the rapid evolution of manufacturing practices introduces new chemicals into environments faster than research can reliably assess their implications. This timing gap leaves practitioners and patients relying on incomplete information for making crucial health decisions. Lastly, the article targets only a slice of reproductive health, potentially overlooking broader systemic health impacts associated with environmental exposures that could also influence reproductive outcomes. **Next Steps** In light of these findings and limitations, the next logical step in research would be to conduct longitudinal and cross-sectional studies focusing on specific chemicals and their direct impact on reproductive health outcomes. These studies should prioritize establishing causal relationships and consider variables such as timing, dosage, and individual susceptibilities to exposure. Additionally, there would be value in increasing research into the effectiveness of different interventions at the personal, community, and policy levels to reduce harmful exposures. Participation in community and policy initiatives should also be investigated to understand the broader social effects. Moreover, exploring the epigenetic changes resulting from exposures and their potential to affect several generations could significantly extend the current research. Investigations into the long-term implications of these epigenetic modifications could help in developing better predictive models for individual risks. Finally, the development of advanced monitoring and diagnostic tools for early detection of environmental pollutant levels in human tissues would augment preventative approaches in healthcare and support more personalized patient guidance. **Conclusion** Di Renzo et al. (2015) have contributed significantly to the field of reproductive health and toxicology by highlighting the insidious threats posed by environmental chemicals. The implications of their study demand concerted attention from expectant mothers, families, young individuals, and healthcare professionals in forming a united front against environmental health hazards. While there are limitations to their findings, such as regional applicability and potential confounding variables, the importance of continued research in this area is unequivocal. The pursuit of deeper insights through more granular studies, interventions, and advanced technology informs the next frontier in safeguarding reproductive health against the backdrop of an increasingly polluted world. This ongoing effort not only has the potential to improve individual health outcomes but will also resonate through public policy, ultimately striving for healthier communities and environments.
